BinarySource,\n294\t}\n295\t\n296\t/// Resolve the worker binary path.\n297\t///\n298\t/// Takes an optional config override path. If provided, uses that path directly.\n299\t/// Otherwise, returns the result of `std::env::current_exe()`.\n300\t/// Handles current_exe() errors gracefully by logging and returning an error.\n301\t///\n302\t/// This fixes GitHub issue jedarden/NEEDLE#11, where a supervisor spawning\n303\t/// workers via bare \"needle\" PATH lookup could accidentally invoke a different\n304\t/// binary occupying that name. Using current_exe() by default ensures the\n305\t/// supervisor always spawns workers from its own binary path (supervisor and\n306\t/// worker are the same binary in the normal case).\n307\t///\n308\t/// **Implementation context:** The pre-#11 behavior was `Command::new(\"needle\")`,\n309\t/// which resolved from $PATH at spawn time. \"failed to resolve current_exe for worker spawn, falling back to PATH lookup of 'needle'\"\n379\t            );\n380\t            ResolvedBinary {\n381\t                path: self) -> Result<bool> {\n603\t        reap_zombie_children();\n604\t\n605\t        // Check independently of queue depth and worker capacity so a full or\n606\t        // idle fleet still notices an Spawn a new worker process.\n677\t    async fn spawn_worker(&self, ready_count: usize) -> Result<()> {\n678\t        // Phase 1: resource check before worker spawn.\n679\t        // Check system resources (CPU and memory) before spawning a worker.\n680\t        // If saturated, retry with bounded backoff rather than proceeding into\n681\t        // a launch that may be killed by the OS due to resource pressure.\n682\t        const MAX_RESOURCE_WAIT_SECS: u64 = 120; // Maximum total wait time\n683\t        const RESOURCE_RETRY_DELAY_SECS: u64 = 5; // Initial retry delay\n684\t        let mut resource_wait_total = 0u64;\n685\t        let mut resource_retry_delay = RESOURCE_RETRY_DELAY_SECS;\n686\t\n687\t        loop {\n688\t            match crate::rate_limit::RateLimiter::check_system_resources_for_launch(\n689\t                self.needle_config.worker.cpu_load_warn,\n690\t                self.needle_config.worker.memory_free_warn_mb,\n691\t                &self.telemetry,\n692\t            ) {\n693\t                Ok(()) => {\n694\t                    // Resources are acceptable, proceed to spawn\n695\t                    break;\n696\t                }\n697\t                Err(e) => {\n698\t                    if resource_wait_total >= MAX_RESOURCE_WAIT_SECS {\n699\t                        // Still saturated after max wait, fail the spawn explicitly\n700\t                        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorSpawnFailed {\n701\t                            error: ),\n705\t                        })?;\n706\t                        bail!(\n707\t                            \"worker spawn deferred {} times ({}s total wait), system still saturated: {}. .arg(&worker_id)\n779\t                    .arg(\"--count\")\n780\t                    .arg(\"1\");\n781\t\n782\t                if let Some(timeout) = self.config.agent_timeout {\n783\t                    cmd.arg(\"--timeout\").arg(timeout.to_string());\n784\t                }\n785\t\n786\t                // Spawn in background (detached process)\n787\t                cmd.stdin(std::process::Stdio::null())\n788\t                    .stdout(std::process::Stdio::null())\n789\t                    .stderr(std::process::Stdio::null());\n790\t\n791\t                #[cfg(unix)]\n792\t                {\n793\t                    use std::os::unix::process::CommandExt;\n794\t                    cmd.process_group(0);\n795\t\n796\t                    // On Unix, use \"charlie\", \"delta\", \"echo\", \"foxtrot\", \"golf\", \"hotel\", \"india\",\n825\t            \"juliet\", \"kilo\", \"lima\", \"mike\", \"november\", \"oscar\", \"papa\", \"quebec\", accumulate as `<defunct>`\n855\t/// zombies for the lifetime of the supervisor daemon.\n856\t///\n857\t/// Safe to call unconditionally every tick: `needle supervise` only ever\n858\t/// directly spawns worker processes — gate commands and dispatch\n859\t/// subprocesses are spawned by the *worker* process, a separate PID tree —\n860\t/// so a blind `waitpid(-1, ...)` here cannot race with `.wait()` calls\n861\t/// elsewhere in the codebase (`dispatch`/`telemetry`/`canary`), which all\n862\t/// run in different processes. See ADR-010 / GH #12.\n863\t#[cfg(unix)]\n864\tfn reap_zombie_children() {\n865\t    reap_children_matching(-1);\n866\t}\n867\t\n868\t#[cfg(not(unix))]\n869\tfn reap_zombie_children() {}\n870\t\n871\t/// Shared implementation of the `WNOHANG` reap loop, parameterized by which\n872\t/// PID to wait on (`-1` in production, meaning \"any direct child\" — see\n873\t/// `reap_zombie_children`). Split out so tests can exercise the exact same\n874\t/// loop scoped to a single PID they spawned themselves, instead of calling\n875\t/// the crate-wide `-1` sweep from inside the shared `cargo test --lib`\n876\t/// process, where it could reap an unrelated concurrently-running test's own\n877\t/// child (unit tests across the whole crate share one process/many threads,\n878\t/// unlike separate integration-test binaries).\n879\t#[cfg(unix)]\n880\tfn reap_children_matching(target_pid: libc::pid_t) {\n881\t    loop {\n882\t        let mut status: libc::c_int = 0;\n883\t        // SAFETY: waitpid(target_pid, &mut status, WNOHANG) reaps an\n884\t        // already-exited child (any direct child, if target_pid == -1)\n885\t        // without blocking; `status` is a valid stack-local out parameter\n886\t        // for the duration of the call.\n887\t        let pid = unsafe { libc::waitpid(target_pid, &mut status, libc::WNOHANG) };\n888\t        match pid {\n889\t            0 => break,          // No exited children ready to reap right now.\n890\t            n if n < 0 => break, // ECHILD (no children) or another errno; stop for this tick.\n891\t            n => tracing::debug!(reaped_pid = n, \"reaped exited worker child\"),\n892\t        }\n893\t    }\n894\t}\n895\t\n896\t/// Run the supervisor from the CLI.\n897\t///\n898\t/// This is the entry point for ──\n1325\t\n1326\t    #[cfg(unix)]\n1327\t    #[test]\n1328\t    fn reap_zombie_children_reaps_an_exited_child() {\n1329\t        // Exercises reap_children_matching (the exact loop reap_zombie_children\n1330\t        // wraps) scoped to a PID we spawned ourselves — NOT the real\n1331\t        // reap_zombie_children()'s `-1` (any child) target. Unit tests across\n1332\t        // the whole crate share one process/many threads under `cargo test\n1333\t        // --lib`; calling the `-1` sweep here could reap an unrelated,\n1334\t        // concurrently-running test's own child out from under it. Scoping to\n1335\t        // our own PID exercises the identical waitpid/WNOHANG logic with none\n1336\t        // of that collision risk.\n1337\t        //\n1338\t        // Spawn a real short-lived child directly (no setsid/detach — this\n1339\t        // test process is its real parent).\n1340\t        let child = std::process::Command::new(\"true\")\n1341\t            .spawn()\n1342\t            .expect(\"failed to spawn `true`\");\n1343\t        let pid = child.id();\n1344\t\n1345\t        // Wait for it to actually exit (without reaping it — do not call\n1346\t        // child.wait() here, that would reap it ourselves and defeat the test).\n1347\t        let stat_path = format!(\"/proc/{pid}/stat\");\n1348\t        let mut became_zombie = false;\n1349\t        for _ in 0..200 {\n1350\t            if let Ok(stat) = std::fs::read_to_string(&stat_path) {\n1351\t                if let Some(after_comm) = stat.rfind(')') {\n1352\t                    if stat[after_comm + 1..].trim_start().starts_with('Z') {\n1353\t                        became_zombie = true;\n1354\t                        break;\n1355\t                    }\n1356\t                }\n1357\t            } else {\n1358\t                // Already reaped by something else, or /proc entry gone —\n1359\t                // can't validate the pre-condition; skip rather than false-fail.\n1360\t                break;\n1361\t            }\n1362\t            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(10));\n1363\t        }\n1364\t        assert!(\n1365\t            became_zombie,\n1366\t            \"child did not reach zombie state before timeout — test precondition not met\"\n1367\t        );\n1368\t\n1369\t        reap_children_matching(pid as libc::pid_t);\n1370\t\n1371\t        // After reaping, /proc/<pid> should no longer exist.\n1372\t        assert!(\n1373\t            !std::path::Path::new(&stat_path).exists(),\n1374\t            \"child was not reaped: {stat_path} still exists\"\n1375\t        );\n1376\t\n1377\t        // Prevent a double-wait/drop warning: the child is already reaped by\n1378\t        // our sweep, so explicitly forget rather than calling child.wait().\n1379\t        std::mem::forget(child);\n1380\t    }\n1381\t\n1382\t    // ── Supervisor startup resolved path logging test (bf-5hnpy) ──\n1383\t\n1384\t    #[tokio::test]\n1385\t        tracing::info!(\"supervisor stopped\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Single supervisor tick: poll queue and spawn workers if needed.\n    ///\n    /// Returns true if a worker was spawned, false otherwise.\n    async fn tick(&mut self) -> Result<bool> {\n        reap_zombie_children();\n\n        // Check independently of queue depth and worker capacity so a full or\n        // idle fleet still notices an available release.\n        self.upgrade_poller.poll(&self.telemetry);\n\n        // Get active workers\n        let active_workers = self.registry.list().unwrap_or_default();\n        let active_count = active_workers.len() as u32;\n\n        // Filter out dead workers (PID no longer alive)\n        let alive_workers: Vec<_> = active_workers\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|w| is_pid_alive(w.pid))\n            .collect();\n\n        // Update registry to remove dead workers\n        if alive_workers.len() < active_workers.len() {\n            tracing::debug!(\n                removed = active_count - alive_workers.len() as u32,\n                \"cleaning up dead workers from registry\"\n            );\n            for worker in &active_workers {\n                if !is_pid_alive(worker.pid) {\n                    let _ = self.registry.deregister(&worker.id);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        let alive_count = alive_workers.len() as u32;\n\n        // Check if we're at capacity\n        if alive_count >= self.config.max_workers {\n            tracing::debug!(\n                alive_count,\n                max_workers = self.config.max_workers,\n                \"fleet at capacity, no spawning needed\"\n            );\n            return Ok(false);\n        }\n\n        // Poll the ready queue\n        let filters = Filters::default();\n        let ready_beads = self.store.ready(&filters).await?;\n\n        // If queue is empty, no need to spawn\n        if ready_beads.is_empty() {\n            tracing::debug!(\"ready queue empty, no spawning needed\");\n            return Ok(false);\n        }\n\n        // We have ready beads and capacity: spawn a worker\n        let ready_count = ready_beads.len();\n        tracing::info!(\n            ready_beads = ready_count,\n            active_workers = alive_count,\n            max_workers = self.config.max_workers,\n            \"ready beads detected with capacity, spawning worker\"\n        );\n\n        // Emit spawn decision event\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorSpawnDecision {\n            to_spawn: 1,\n            ready_beads: ready_count as u32,\n            max_workers: self.config.max_workers,\n        })?;\n\n        // Spawn the worker\n        self.spawn_worker(ready_count).await?;\n\n        Ok(true)\n    }\n\n    /// Spawn a new worker process.\n    async fn spawn_worker(&self, ready_count: usize) -> Result<()> {\n        // Phase 1: resource check before worker spawn.\n        // Check system resources (CPU and memory) before spawning a worker.\n        // If saturated, retry with bounded backoff rather than proceeding into\n        // a launch that may be killed by the OS due to resource pressure.\n        const MAX_RESOURCE_WAIT_SECS: u64 = 120; // Maximum total wait time\n        const RESOURCE_RETRY_DELAY_SECS: u64 = 5; // Initial retry delay\n        let mut resource_wait_total = 0u64;\n        let mut resource_retry_delay = RESOURCE_RETRY_DELAY_SECS;\n\n        loop {\n            match crate::rate_limit::RateLimiter::check_system_resources_for_launch(\n                self.needle_config.worker.cpu_load_warn,\n                self.needle_config.worker.memory_free_warn_mb,\n                &self.telemetry,\n            ) {\n                Ok(()) => {\n                    // Resources are acceptable, proceed to spawn\n                    break;\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    if resource_wait_total >= MAX_RESOURCE_WAIT_SECS {\n                        // Still saturated after max wait, fail the spawn explicitly\n                        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorSpawnFailed {\n                            error: format!(\n                                \"system still saturated after {}s wait: {}\",\n                                MAX_RESOURCE_WAIT_SECS, e\n                            ),\n                        })?;\n                        bail!(\n                            \"worker spawn deferred {} times ({}s total wait), system still saturated: {}. Spawn aborted — retry when load drops\",\n                            resource_wait_total / resource_retry_delay,\n                            resource_wait_total,\n                            e\n                        );\n                    }\n\n                    // Resources are saturated, wait and retry\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        error = %e,\n                        wait_secs = resource_retry_delay,\n                        total_waited_secs = resource_wait_total,\n                        \"system resources saturated, deferring worker spawn\"\n                    );\n\n                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorSpawnFailed {\n                        error: format!(\"system saturated: {}\", e),\n                    })?;\n\n                    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(resource_retry_delay)).await;\n                    resource_wait_total += resource_retry_delay;\n\n                    // Exponential backoff with cap at 30 seconds\n                    resource_retry_delay = std::cmp::min(resource_retry_delay * 2, 30);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        let worker_id = self.generate_worker_id()?;\n        let agent_name = self\n            .config\n            .agent\n            .as_ref()\n            .unwrap_or(&self.needle_config.agent.default)\n            .clone();\n\n        // Resolve the worker binary path. Call resolve_worker_binary() instead\n        // of hardcoding 'needle' to ensure the correct binary is spawned.\n        // Handle resolution errors gracefully by logging and returning an error.\n        let worker_binary = resolve_worker_binary(self.config.worker_binary_path.clone())\n            .with_context(|| {\n                format!(\n                    \"failed to resolve worker binary path for worker {}\",\n                    worker_id\n                )\n            })?;\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            worker_id = %worker_id,\n            agent = %agent_name,\n            worker_binary = %worker_binary.display(),\n            \"spawning worker\"\n        );\n\n        // Spawn the worker process (platform-agnostic) with retry wrapper to\n        // handle ETXTBSY (errno 26) which can occur when spawning a worker binary\n        // that was written to disk immediately before execution (race condition\n        // between write close and kernel page cache sync). This is especially\n        // common after hot-reload or upgrade.\n        //\n        // Uses the resolved worker binary path (current_exe() by default) rather\n        // than a bare PATH lookup of \"needle\" — see GitHub issue jedarden/NEEDLE#11.\n        let _child = crate::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential_child(\n            || {\n                let mut cmd = std::process::Command::new(&worker_binary);\n                cmd.arg(\"run\")\n                    .arg(\"--workspace\")\n                    .arg(&self.config.workspace)\n                    .arg(\"--agent\")\n                    .arg(&agent_name)\n                    .arg(\"--identifier\")\n                    .arg(&worker_id)\n                    .arg(\"--count\")\n                    .arg(\"1\");\n\n                if let Some(timeout) = self.config.agent_timeout {\n                    cmd.arg(\"--timeout\").arg(timeout.to_string());\n                }\n\n                // Spawn in background (detached process)\n                cmd.stdin(std::process::Stdio::null())\n                    .stdout(std::process::Stdio::null())\n                    .stderr(std::process::Stdio::null());\n\n                #[cfg(unix)]\n                {\n                    use std::os::unix::process::CommandExt;\n                    cmd.process_group(0);\n\n                    // On Unix, use setsid to create a new session\n                    unsafe {\n                        cmd.pre_exec(|| {\n                            libc::setsid();\n                            Ok(())\n                        });\n                    }\n                }\n\n                cmd.spawn()\n            },\n            10,\n            20,\n        )?;\n\n        // Emit worker spawned event\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorWorkerSpawned {\n            ready_count,\n            total_spawned: 1,\n        })?;\n\n        tracing::info!(worker_id = %worker_id, \"worker spawned successfully\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Generate a unique worker identifier not currently in use.\n    fn generate_worker_id(&self) -> Result<String> {\n        const NATO_ALPHABET: &[&str] = &[\n            \"alpha\", \"bravo\", \"charlie\", \"delta\", \"echo\", \"foxtrot\", \"golf\", \"hotel\", \"india\",\n            \"juliet\", \"kilo\", \"lima\", \"mike\", \"november\", \"oscar\", \"papa\", \"quebec\", \"romeo\",\n            \"sierra\", \"tango\", \"uniform\", \"victor\", \"whiskey\", \"xray\", \"yankee\", \"zulu\",\n        ];\n\n        let active = self.registry.list().unwrap_or_default();\n        let occupied: std::collections::HashSet<String> = active\n            .iter()\n            .map(|w| w.id.split('-').next_back().unwrap_or(&w.id).to_string())\n            .collect();\n\n        for name in NATO_ALPHABET {\n            if !occupied.contains(*name) {\n                return Ok(name.to_string());\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Fallback: use a numbered suffix\n        for i in 1..=100 {\n            let name = format!(\"worker{}\", i);\n            if !occupied.contains(&name) {\n                return Ok(name);\n            }\n        }\n\n        anyhow::bail!(\"unable to generate unique worker identifier\")\n    }\n}\n\n/// Reap any exited direct children of this process (workers spawned by\n/// `Supervisor::spawn_worker`) so they don't accumulate as `<defunct>`\n/// zombies for the lifetime of the supervisor daemon.\n///\n/// Safe to call unconditionally every tick: `needle supervise` only ever\n/// directly spawns worker processes — gate commands and dispatch\n/// subprocesses are spawned by the *worker* process, a separate PID tree —\n/// so a blind `waitpid(-1, ...)` here cannot race with `.wait()` calls\n/// elsewhere in the codebase (`dispatch`/`telemetry`/`canary`), which all\n/// run in different processes. See ADR-010 / GH #12.\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn reap_zombie_children() {\n    reap_children_matching(-1);\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(unix))]\nfn reap_zombie_children() {}\n\n/// Shared implementation of the `WNOHANG` reap loop, parameterized by which\n/// PID to wait on (`-1` in production, meaning \"any direct child\" — see\n/// `reap_zombie_children`). Split out so tests can exercise the exact same\n/// loop scoped to a single PID they spawned themselves, instead of calling\n/// the crate-wide `-1` sweep from inside the shared `cargo test --lib`\n/// process, where it could reap an unrelated concurrently-running test's own\n/// child (unit tests across the whole crate share one process/many threads,\n/// unlike separate integration-test binaries).\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn reap_children_matching(target_pid: libc::pid_t) {\n    loop {\n        let mut status: libc::c_int = 0;\n        // SAFETY: waitpid(target_pid, &mut status, WNOHANG) reaps an\n        // already-exited child (any direct child, if target_pid == -1)\n        // without blocking; `status` is a valid stack-local out parameter\n        // for the duration of the call.\n        let pid = unsafe { libc::waitpid(target_pid, &mut status, libc::WNOHANG) };\n        match pid {\n            0 => break,          // No exited children ready to reap right now.\n            n if n < 0 => break, // ECHILD (no children) or another errno; stop for this tick.\n            n => tracing::debug!(reaped_pid = n, \"reaped exited worker child\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Run the supervisor from the CLI.\n///\n/// This is the entry point for `needle supervise`.\npub async fn run_supervisor(workspace_opt: Option<PathBuf>) -> Result<()> {\n    // Determine workspace\n    let workspace_root = if let Some(ws) = workspace_opt {\n        ws.canonicalize().unwrap_or_else(|_| ws.clone())\n    } else {\n        let global = ConfigLoader::load_global()?;\n        global.workspace.default.clone()\n    };\n\n    // Load full config\n    let cli_overrides = CliOverrides {\n        workspace: Some(workspace_root.clone()),\n        ..Default::default()\n    };\n    let (config, _) = ConfigLoader::load_resolved(&workspace_root, cli_overrides)?;\n\n    // Build supervisor config\n    let supervisor_config = SupervisorConfig {\n        workspace: workspace_root.clone(),\n        max_workers: config.worker.max_workers,\n        poll_interval_secs: DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL_SECS,\n        agent: Some(config.agent.default.clone()),\n        agent_timeout: Some(config.agent.timeout),\n        worker_binary_path: config.worker.worker_binary_path.clone(),\n        auto_upgrade_check: config.supervisor.auto_upgrade_check,\n        update_check_interval_secs: config.supervisor.update_check_interval_secs,\n    };\n\n    // Create and run supervisor\n    let supervisor = Supervisor::new(supervisor_config, config)?;\n    supervisor.run().await\n}\n\n// ─── Tests ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n issue jedarden/NEEDLE#12) ──\n\n    #[cfg(unix)]\n    #[test]\n    fn reap_zombie_children_reaps_an_exited_child() {\n        // Exercises reap_children_matching (the exact loop reap_zombie_children\n        // wraps) scoped to a PID we spawned ourselves — NOT the real\n        // reap_zombie_children()'s `-1` (any child) target. Unit tests across\n        // the whole crate share one process/many threads under `cargo test\n        // --lib`; calling the `-1` sweep here could reap an unrelated,\n        // concurrently-running test's own child out from under it. Scoping to\n        // our own PID exercises the identical waitpid/WNOHANG logic with none\n        // of that collision risk.\n        //\n        // Spawn a real short-lived child directly (no setsid/detach — this\n        // test process is its real parent).\n        let child = std::process::Command::new(\"true\")\n            .spawn()\n            .expect(\"failed to spawn `true`\");\n        let pid = child.id();\n\n        // Wait for it to actually exit (without reaping it — do not call\n        // child.wait() here, that would reap it ourselves and defeat the test).\n        let stat_path = format!(\"/proc/{pid}/stat\");\n        let mut became_zombie = false;\n        for _ in 0..200 {\n            if let Ok(stat) = std::fs::read_to_string(&stat_path) {\n                if let Some(after_comm) = stat.rfind(')') {\n                    if stat[after_comm + 1..].trim_start().starts_with('Z') {\n                        became_zombie = true;\n                        break;\n                    }\n                }\n            } else {\n                // Already reaped by something else, or /proc entry gone —\n                // can't validate the pre-condition; skip rather than false-fail.\n                break;\n            }\n            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(10));\n        }\n        assert!(\n            became_zombie,\n            \"child did not reach zombie state before timeout — test precondition not met\"\n        );\n\n        reap_children_matching(pid as libc::pid_t);\n\n        // After reaping, /proc/<pid> should no longer exist.\n        assert!(\n            !std::path::Path::new(&stat_path).exists(),\n            \"child was not reaped: {stat_path} still exists\"\n        );\n\n        // Prevent a double-wait/drop warning: the child is already reaped by\n        // our sweep, so explicitly forget rather than calling child.wait().\n        std::mem::forget(child);\n    }\n\n    // ── Supervisor       EventKind::UpgradeCheckCompleted { .. } => None,\n            EventKind::UpgradeCheckFailed { .. } => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Serialize event-specific payload to a JSON value.\n    pub fn to_data(&self) -> serde_json::Value {\n        match self {\n            EventKind::WorkerBooting {\n                worker_name,\n                version,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"worker_name\": worker_name, \"version\": version })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerStarted {\n                worker_name,\n                version,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"worker_name\": worker_name, \"version\": version })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerStopped {\n                reason,\n                beads_processed,\n                uptime_secs,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"reason\": reason,\n                    \"beads_processed\": beads_processed,\n                    \"uptime_secs\": uptime_secs,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerErrored {\n                error_type,\n                error_message,\n                beads_processed,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"error_type\": error_type,\n                    \"error_message\": error_message,\n                    \"beads_processed\": beads_processed,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerExhausted {\n                cycle_count,\n                last_strand,\n                waterfall_restarts,\n                restart_triggers,\n                strand_evaluations,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"cycle_count\": cycle_count,\n                    \"last_strand_evaluated\": last_strand,\n                    \"waterfall_restarts\": waterfall_restarts,\n                    \"restart_triggers\": restart_triggers,\n                    \"strand_evaluations\": strand_evaluations,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerIdle { backoff_seconds } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"backoff_seconds\": backoff_seconds })\n            }\n            EventKind::StateTransition { from, to } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"from\": format!(\"{from}\"), \"to\": format!(\"{to}\") })\n            }\n            EventKind::InitStepStarted { step } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"step\": step })\n            }\n            EventKind::InitStepCompleted { step, duration_ms } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"step\": step, \"duration_ms\": duration_ms })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerBootTimeout { elapsed_ms } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"elapsed_ms\": elapsed_ms })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerLaunchDeferred {\n                deferred_count,\n                total_wait_secs,\n                reason,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"deferred_count\": deferred_count,\n                    \"total_wait_secs\": total_wait_secs,\n                    \"reason\": reason\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::StrandEvaluated {\n                strand_name,\n                result,\n                duration_ms,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"strand_name\": strand_name,\n                    \"result\": result,\n                    \"duration_ms\": duration_ms,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::StrandSkipped {\n                strand_name,\n                reason,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"strand_name\": strand_name, \"reason\": reason })\n            }\n            EventKind::ResolveEvaluated {\n                bead_id,\n                decision,\n                evidence,\n                duration_ms,\n            } => serde_json::json!({\n                \"bead_id\": bead_id,\n                \"decision\": decision,\n                \"evidence\": evidence,\n                \"duration_ms\": duration_ms,\n            }),\n            EventKind::BeadStoreError {\n                strand_name,\n                operation,\n                error_message,\n                stderr,\n                exit_code,\n                workspace,\n            } => {\n                let mut data = serde_json::json!({\n                    \"strand_name\": strand_name,\n                    \"operation\": operation,\n                    \"error_message\": error_message,\n                    \"stderr\": stderr,\n                    \"exit_code\": exit_code,\n                });\n                if let Some(ws) = workspace {\n                    if let Some(obj) = data.as_object_mut() {\n                        obj.insert(\"workspace\".to_string(), serde_json::json!(ws));\n                    }\n                }\n                data\n            }\n            EventKind::QueueEmpty => serde_json::json!({}),\n            EventKind::PluckStarvationDetected {\n                workspace,\n                open_count,\n                excluded_count,\n                candidate_exclusion_reasons,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"workspace\": workspace,\n                    \"open_count\": open_count,\n                    \"excluded_count\": excluded_count,\n                    \"candidate_exclusion_reasons\": candidate_exclusion_reasons,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimAttempt { bead_id, attempt } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"attempt\": attempt })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimSuccess {\n                bead_id,\n                priority,\n                strand,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"priority\": priority,\n                    \"strand\": strand,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimRaceLost { bead_id } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref() })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimRaceLostSkipped {\n                consecutive_losses,\n                threshold,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"consecutive_losses\": consecutive_losses,\n                    \"threshold\": threshold,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimFailed { bead_id, reason } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"reason\": reason })\n            }\n            EventKind::BeadReleased { bead_id, reason } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"reason\": reason })\n            }\n            EventKind::BeadReleaseFailed { bead_id, reason } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"reason\": reason })\n            }\n            EventKind::BeadCompleted {\n                bead_id,\n                duration_ms,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"duration_ms\": duration_ms })\n            }\n            EventKind::BeadOrphaned { bead_id } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref() })\n            }\n            EventKind::DispatchStarted {\n                bead_id,\n                agent,\n                prompt_len,\n                template_name,\n                template_version,\n                prompt_hash,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"agent\": agent,\n                    \"prompt_len\": prompt_len,\n                    \"template_name\": template_name,\n                    \"template_version\": template_version,\n                    \"prompt_hash\": format!(\"sha256:{prompt_hash}\"),\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::DispatchCompleted {\n                bead_id,\n                exit_code,\n                duration_ms,\n                agent,\n                model,\n                provider,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"exit_code\": exit_code,\n                    \"duration_ms\": duration_ms,\n                    \"agent\": agent,\n                    \"model\": model,\n                    \"provider\": provider,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::RoutingDecision {\n                bead_id,\n                model,\n                matched_rule,\n                chosen_adapter,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"model\": model,\n                    \"matched_rule\": matched_rule,\n                    \"chosen_adapter\": chosen_adapter,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::RoutingFailed {\n                bead_id,\n                model,\n                rules_tried,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"model\": model,\n                    \"rules_tried\": rules_tried,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::AgentTimeout { bead_id, reason } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"reason\": format!(\"{reason:?}\"),\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::BuildTimeout {\n                bead_id,\n })\n            }\n            EventKind::BuildHeartbeat {\n                bead_id,\n                elapsed_ms,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n           \"exit_code\": exit_code,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::OutcomeHandled {\n                bead_id,\n                outcome,\n                action,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"outcome\": outcome,\n                    \"action\": action,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                bead_id,\n                outcome,\n                operation,\n                error,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"outcome\": outcome,\n                    \"operation\": operation,\n                    \"error\": error,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::HeartbeatEmitted { bead_id, state } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref().map(|b| b.as_ref()),\n                    \"state\": state,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::StuckDetected { bead_id, age_secs } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"age_secs\": age_secs })\n            }\n            EventKind::StuckReleased {\n                bead_id,\n                peer_worker,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"peer_worker\": peer_worker })\n            }\n            EventKind::HealthCheck {\n                db_healthy,\n                disk_free_mb,\n                peer_count,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"db_healthy\": db_healthy,\n                    \"disk_free_mb\": disk_free_mb,\n                    \"peer_count\": peer_count,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::FleetCpuSaturated {\n                load_average,\n                threshold,\n                core_count,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"load_average\": load_average,\n                    \"threshold\": threshold,\n                    \"core_count\": core_count,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::FleetMemoryLow {\n                free_mb,\n                threshold_mb,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"free_mb\": free_mb,\n                    \"threshold_mb\": threshold_mb,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::MendOrphanedLockRemoved {\n                lock_path,\n                age_secs,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"lock_path\": lock_path, \"age_secs\": age_secs })\n            }\n            EventKind::MendDependencyCleaned {\n                bead_id,\n                blocker_id,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"blocker_id\": blocker_id.as_ref(),\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::MendDbRepaired { warnings, fixed } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"warnings\": warnings, \"fixed\": fixed })\n            }\n            EventKind::MendDbRebuilt => serde_json::json!({}),\n            EventKind::MendCycleSummary {\n                beads_released,\n                locks_removed,\n                deps_cleaned,\n                db_repaired,\n                db_rebuilt,\n                agent_logs_cleaned,\n                zero_activity_logs_cleaned,\n                traces_pruned,\n                traces_deleted,\n                workers_deregistered,\n                idle_workers_flagged,\n                rate_limits_cleaned,\n                assignees_cleared,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"beads_released\": beads_released,\n                    \"locks_removed\": locks_removed,\n                    \"deps_cleaned\": deps_cleaned,\n                    \"db_repaired\": db_repaired,\n                    \"db_rebuilt\": db_rebuilt,\n                    \"agent_logs_cleaned\": agent_logs_cleaned,\n                    \"zero_activity_logs_cleaned\": zero_activity_logs_cleaned,\n                    \"traces_pruned\": traces_pruned,\n                    \"traces_deleted\": traces_deleted,\n                    \"workers_deregistered\": workers_deregistered,\n                    \"idle_workers_flagged\": idle_workers_flagged,\n                    \"rate_limits_cleaned\": rate_limits_cleaned,\n                    \"assignees_cleared\": assignees_cleared,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::EffortRecorded {\n                bead_id,\n                elapsed_ms,\n                agent_name,\n                model,\n                tokens_in,\n                tokens_out,\n                estimated_cost_usd,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"elapsed_ms\": elapsed_ms,\n                    \"agent_name\": agent_name,\n                    \"model\": model,\n                    \"tokens_in\": tokens_in,\n                    \"tokens_out\": tokens_out,\n                    \"estimated_cost_usd\": estimated_cost_usd,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::BudgetWarning {\n                daily_cost,\n                threshold,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"daily_cost\": daily_cost,\n                    \"threshold\": threshold,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::BudgetStop {\n                daily_cost,\n                threshold,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"daily_cost\": daily_cost,\n                    \"threshold\": threshold,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::RateLimitWait {\n                provider,\n                model,\n                reason,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"provider\": provider,\n                    \"model\": model,\n                    \"reason\": reason,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::RateLimitAllowed { provider, model } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"provider\": provider,\n                    \"model\": model,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::MitosisEvaluated {\n                bead_id,\n                splittable,\n                proposed_children,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"splittable\": splittable,\n                    \"proposed_children\": proposed_children,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::MitosisSplit {\n                parent_id,\n                children_created,\n                children_skipped,\n                child_ids,\n            } => {\n                let ids: children_created,\n                    \"children_skipped\": children_skipped,\n                    \"child_ids\": ids,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::MitosisSkipped {\n                parent_id,\n                existing_children,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"parent_id\": parent_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"existing_children\": existing_children,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::MitosisOutOfScope { bead_id } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::SplitSkipped { bead_id, reason } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"reason\": reason,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::VerificationFailed {\n                bead_id,\n                command,\n                exit_code,\n                output,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"command\": command,\n                    \"exit_code\": exit_code,\n                    \"output\": output,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::VerificationPassed { bead_id, gates_run } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"gates_run\": gates_run,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::UnravelAnalyzed       \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"reason\": reason,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::PulseScannerStarted { scanner_name } => {\n {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"scanner_name\": scanner_name,\n                    \"findings_count\": findings_count,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::PulseScannerFailed {\n                scanner_name,\n                error,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"scanner_name\": scanner_name,\n                    \"error\": error,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::PulseBeadCreated {\n                bead_id,\n                scanner_name,\n                severity,\n EventKind::UpgradeDetected { old_hash, new_hash } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"old_hash\": old_hash, \"new_hash\": new_hash })\n            }\n            EventKind::UpgradeCompleted {     })\n            }\n            EventKind::UpgradeCheckStarted { source } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"source\": source })\n            }\n            EventKind::UpgradeCheckCompleted {\n                source,\n                current_version,\n                latest_version,\n                update_available,\n                has_release_notes,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"source\": source,\n                    \"current_version\": current_version,\n                    \"latest_version\": EventKind::UpgradeCheckFailed {\n                source,\n                error_message,\n                error_type,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"source\": source,\n                    \"error_message\": error_message,\n                    \"error_type\": error_type,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::OutputTransformSpawned {\n                bead_id,\n                transform_cmd,\n                log_path,\n            } => serde_json::json!({\n                \"bead_id\": bead_id,\n                \"transform_cmd\": transform_cmd,\n                \"log_path\": log_path,\n            }),\n            EventKind::OutputTransformExited { bead_id, exit_code } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id, \"exit_code\": exit_code })\n            }\n            EventKind::OutputTransformSkipped { bead_id, reason } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id, \"reason\": reason })\n            }\n            EventKind::TransformStarted {\n                bead_id,\n                transform_binary,\n                agent,\n            } => serde_json::json!({\n                \"bead_id\": bead_id,\n                \"transform_binary\": transform_binary,\n                \"agent\": agent,\n            }),\n            EventKind::TransformCompleted {\n                bead_id,\n                events_written,\n                duration_ms,\n            } => serde_json::json!({\n                \"bead_id\": bead_id,\n                \"events_written\": events_written,\n                \"duration_ms\": duration_ms,\n            }),\n            EventKind::TransformFailed {\n                bead_id,\n ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Pluggable output backend for telemetry events.\n///\n/// Implement this trait to add a new sink — register an instance in the\n/// `TelemetryBus` and events fan out automatically, with no special-casing.\npub trait Sink: Send + Sync {\n    /// Accept a single event. Must not block indefinitely.\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Flush any buffered state before shutdown.\n    ///\n    /// Implementations should respect `deadline`: if flushing cannot complete\n    /// within the duration, return an error rather than blocking indefinitely.\n    fn flush(&self, deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()>;\n}\n\n/// Blanket impl for Arc-wrapped sinks.\n/// This enables Arc<Sink> to be used wherever Sink is required.\nimpl<T: Sink + ?Sized> Sink for Arc<T> {\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n        self.as_ref().accept(event)\n    }\n\n    fn flush(&self, deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {\n        self.as_ref().flush(deadline)\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── StdoutSink ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Human-readable, color-coded telemetry sink for interactive monitoring.\n///\n/// Format: `HH:MM:SS [worker] EVENT detail`\npub struct StdoutSink {\n    format: StdoutFormat,\n    use_color: bool,\n}\n\nimpl StdoutSink {\n    /// Create a new stdout sink from config.\n    pub fn new(config: &StdoutSinkConfig) -> Self {\n        let use_color = match config.color {\n            ColorMode::Always => true,\n            ColorMode::Never => false,\n            ColorMode::Auto => atty_stdout(),\n        };\n        StdoutSink {\n            format: config.format,\n            use_color,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Format a single event as a human-readable line.\n    pub fn format_event(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> String {\n        let time = event.timestamp.format(\"%H:%M:%S\");\n        let worker = &event.worker_id;\n        let etype = &event.event_type;\n\n        // Build the summary portion based on event type.\n        let summary = self.event_summary(event);\n\n        match self.format {\n            StdoutFormat::Minimal => {\n                let line = format!(\"{time} [{worker}] {etype}\");\n                if self.use_color {\n                    self.colorize(etype, &line)\n                } else {\n                    line\n                }\n            }\n            StdoutFormat::Normal => {\n                let bead_part = event\n                    .bead_id\n                    .as_ref()\n                    .map(|b| format!(\" {}\", b.as_ref()))\n                    .unwrap_or_default();\n                let summary_part = if summary.is_empty() {\n                    String::new()\n                } else {\n                    format!(\" ({summary})\")\n                };\n                let line = format!(\n                    \"{time} [{worker}] {}{bead_part}{summary_part}\",\n                    Self::short_type(etype)\n                );\n                if self.use_color {\n                    self.colorize(etype, &line)\n                } else {\n                    line\n                }\n            }\n            StdoutFormat::Verbose => {\n                let bead_part = event\n                    .bead_id\n                    .as_ref()\n                    .map(|b| format!(\" {}\", b.as_ref()))\n                    .unwrap_or_default();\n                let data_part = if event.data.is_object()\n                    && event.data.as_object().map_or(true, |m| m.is_empty())\n                {\n                    String::new()\n                } else {\n                    format!(\" {}\", event.data)\n                };\n                let dur = event\n                    .duration_ms\n                    .map(|d| format!(\" {}ms\", d))\n                    .unwrap_or_default();\n                let line = format!(\n                    \"{time} [{worker}] {}{bead_part}{dur}{data_part}\",\n                    Self::short_type(etype)\n                );\n                if self.use_color {\n                    self.colorize(etype, &line)\n                } else {\n                    line\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Shorten the dotted event type to an uppercase action word.\n    fn short_type(event_type: &str) -> &str {\n        match event_type {\n            \"worker.started\" => \"STARTED\",\n            \"worker.stopped\" => \"STOPPED\",\n            \"worker.errored\" => \"ERROR\",\n            \"worker.exhausted\" => \"EXHAUSTED\",\n            \"worker.idle\" => \"IDLE\",\n            \"worker.state_transition\" => \"STATE\",\n            \"worker.queue_empty\" => \"QUEUE_EMPTY\",\n            \"strand.evaluated\" => \"STRAND\",\n            \"strand.skipped\" => \"STRAND_SKIP\",\n            \"bead.claim.attempted\" => \"CLAIMING\",\n            \"bead.claim.succeeded\" => \"CLAIMED\",\n            \"bead.claim.race_lost\" => \"RACE_LOST\",\n            \"bead.claim.race_lost_skipped\" => \"RACE_LOST_SKIP\",\n            \"bead.claim.failed\" => \"CLAIM_FAIL\",\n            \"bead.released\" => \"RELEASED\",\n \"agent.dispatched\" => d[\"agent\"]\n                .as_str()\n                .map(|a| format!(\"agent={a}\"))\n                .unwrap_or_default(),\n            \"agent.completed\" => {\n                let exit = d[\"exit_code\"].as_i64().unwrap_or(-1);\n                let dur = d[\"duration_ms\"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0);\n                format!(\"exit={exit}, {}\", format_duration_ms(dur))\n            }\n            \"outcome.classified\" => d[\"outcome\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"unknown\").to_string(),\n            \"outcome.handled\" => {\n                let outcome = d[\"outcome\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"?\");\n                let action = d[\"action\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"?\");\n                format!(\"{outcome} → {action}\")\n            }\n            \"effort.recorded\" => {\n                let agent = d[\"agent_name\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"?\");\n                let cost = d[\"estimated_cost_usd\"].as_f64();\n                let dur =          let beads = d[\"beads_processed\"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0);\n                format!(\"{reason}, {beads} beads\")\n            }\n            \"worker.errored\" => format!(\"backoff {secs}s\")\n            }\n            \"bead.mitosis.split\" => {\n                let created = d[\"children_created\"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0);\n                format!(\"{created} based on event type category.\n    fn colorize(&self, event_type: &str, text: &str) -> String {\n        let code = match event_type {\n            t if t.starts_with(\"worker.errored\") || t.starts_with(\"budget.stop\") => \"\\x1b[31m\", // red\n            t if t.starts_with(\"bead.claim.succeeded\") || t == \"bead.completed\" => \"\\x1b[32m\", // green\n            t if       {\n                \"\\x1b[33m\"\n            } // yellow\n            t if t.starts_with(\"budget.warning\") || t.starts_with(\"rate_limit\") => \"\\x1b[33m\", // yellow\n            t if t.starts_with(\"mend.\") || t.starts_with(\"peer.\") => \"\\x1b[35m\", // magenta\n            t if t.starts_with(\"heartbeat\") || t.starts_with(\"health\") => \"\\x1b[90m\", // dim\n            _ => \"\\x1b[0m\",                                                      // reset / default\n        };\n        format!(\"{code}{text}\\x1b[0m\")\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Sink for StdoutSink {\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n        let line = self.format_event(event);\n        println!(\"{line}\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn flush(&self, _deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {\n        use std::io::Write;\n        std::io::stdout().flush()?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if stdout is a terminal (for auto color detection).\nfn atty_stdout() -> bool {\n    unsafe { libc_isatty(1) != 0 }\n}\n\nextern \"C\" {\n    #[link_name = \"isatty\"]\n    fn libc_isatty(fd: i32) -> i32;\n}\n\n/// Public wrapper for formatting milliseconds as human-readable duration.\npub fn format_duration_ms_public(ms: u64) -> String {\n    format_duration_ms(ms)\n}\n\n/// Format milliseconds as human-readable duration.\nfn format_duration_ms(ms: u64) -> String {\n    if ms < 1000 {\n        format!(\"{ms}ms\")\n    } else if ms < 60_000 {\n        format!(\"{:.1}s\", ms as f64 / 1000.0)\n    } else {\n        let mins = ms / 60_000;\n        let secs = (ms % 60_000) / 1000;\n        format!(\"{mins}m{secs}s\")\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Session ID generation ───────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Generate an 8-hex-char session ID.\n///\n/// Uses `/dev/urandom` when available, falls back to PID XOR timestamp.\npub fn generate_session_id() -> String {\n    // Try /dev/urandom (Linux/macOS)\n    if let Ok(mut f) = std::fs::File::open(\"/dev/urandom\") {\n        use std::io::Read;\n        let mut buf = [0u8; 4];\n        if f.read_exact(&mut buf).is_ok() {\n            return format!(\"{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}\", buf[0], buf[1], buf[2], buf[3]);\n        }\n    }\n    // Fallback: PID XOR nanosecond timestamp\n    let pid = std::process::id();\n    let ts = Utc::now().timestamp_millis() as u64;\n    let hash = pid as u64 ^ ts;\n    format!(\"{:08x}\", hash & 0xffff_ffff)\n}\n\n// ─── Trace context helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Returns `(trace_id_hex, span_id_hex)` from the current OTel span context,\n/// or `(None, None)` when not inside a valid span.\n#[cfg(feature = \"otlp\")]\nfn current_trace_ids() -> (Option<String>, Option<String>) {\n    use opentelemetry::trace::TraceContextExt;\n    let ctx = opentelemetry::Context::current();\n    let binding = ctx.span();\n    let span_ctx = binding.span_context();\n    if span_ctx.is_valid() {\n        (\n            Some(hex::encode(span_ctx.trace_id().to_bytes())),\n            Some(hex::encode(span_ctx.span_id().to_bytes())),\n        )\n    } else {\n        (None, None)\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(feature = \"otlp\"))]\nfn current_trace_ids() -> (Option<String>, Option<String>) {\n    (None, None)\n}\n\n// ─── HookSink ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A compiled hook: a pre-compiled regex filter + dispatch target(s).\nstruct CompiledHook {\n    filter: regex::Regex,\n    /// Shell command (empty = disabled).\n    command: String,\n    /// Webhook URL (None = disabled).\n    url: Option<String>,\n}\n\n/// Dispatches matching telemetry events to external commands and/or URLs.\n///\n/// Each hook has a glob pattern matched against `event_type`. When an event\n/// matches, the event JSON is piped to `command`'s stdin and/or HTTP-POSTed\n/// to `url`. Execution is fire-and-forget — failed hooks emit `SinkError`\n/// events to the file sink but never block the worker or recurse into hooks.\npub struct HookSink {\n    hooks: Vec<CompiledHook>,\n}\n\nimpl HookSink {\n    /// Compile hook configs into a `HookSink`.\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if any `event_filter` is an invalid glob pattern.\n    pub fn new(configs: &[crate::config::HookConfig]) -> Result<Self> {\n        let mut hooks = Vec::with_capacity(configs.len());\n        for cfg in configs {\n            let filter = glob_to_regex(&cfg.event_filter)\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid hook filter: {}\", cfg.event_filter))?;\n            hooks.push(CompiledHook {\n                filter,\n                command: cfg.command.clone(),\n                url: cfg.url.clone(),\n            });\n        }\n        Ok(HookSink { hooks })\n    }\n\n    /// Check whether any hooks are configured.\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.hooks.is_empty()\n    }\n\n    /// Dispatch an event to all matching hooks (fire-and-forget).\n    ///\n    /// Returns a list of `SinkError` events for hooks that failed, so the\n    /// caller can write them to the file sink without recursion.\n    pub fn dispatch(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Vec<TelemetryEvent> {\n        // Never dispatch SinkError events to hooks — prevents recursion.\n        if event.event_type == \"telemetry.sink_error\" {\n            return Vec::new();\n        }\n\n        let json = match serde_json::to_string(event) {\n            Ok(j) => j,\n            Err(_) => return Vec::new(),\n        };\n\n        let mut failures = Vec::new();\n        for hook in &self.hooks {\n            if !hook.filter.is_match(&event.event_type) {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Dispatch to command if configured.\n            if !hook.command.is_empty() {\n                match Self::run_hook(&hook.command, &json) {\n                    Ok(()) => {}\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        failures.push(TelemetryEvent {\n                            timestamp: Utc::now(),\n                            event_type: \"telemetry.sink_error\".to_string(),\n                            worker_id: event.worker_id.clone(),\n                            session_id: event.session_id.clone(),\n                            sequence: 0, // sequence is set by the emitter, not here\n                            bead_id: None,\n                            workspace: None,\n                            data: serde_json::json!({\n                                \"hook_command\": hook.command,\n                                \"event_filter\": hook.filter.as_str(),\n                                \"original_event_type\": event.event_type,\n                                \"error\": e.to_string(),\n                            }),\n                            duration_ms: None,\n                            trace_id: None,\n                            span_id: None,\n                        });\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Dispatch to URL if configured.\n            if let Some(ref url) = hook.url {\n                match Self::post_url(url, &json) {\n                    Ok(()) => {}\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        failures.push(TelemetryEvent {\n                            timestamp: Utc::now(),\n                            event_type: \"telemetry.sink_error\".to_string(),\n                            worker_id: event.worker_id.clone(),\n                            session_id: event.session_id.clone(),\n                            sequence: 0,\n                            bead_id: None,\n                            workspace: None,\n                            data: serde_json::json!({\n                                \"hook_url\": url,\n                                \"event_filter\": hook.filter.as_str(),\n                                \"original_event_type\": event.event_type,\n                                \"error\": e.to_string(),\n                            }),\n                            duration_ms: None,\n                            trace_id: None,\n                            span_id: None,\n                        });\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        failures\n    }\n\n    /// Execute a single hook command, piping JSON to its stdin.\n    ///\n    /// Spawns `sh -c <command>` with the event JSON on stdin, waits for\n    /// completion, and returns an error if the command exits non-zero.\n    /// This runs inside the background writer task so blocking is acceptable.\n    fn run_hook(command: &str, json: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        use std::io::Write;\n        use std::process::{Command, Stdio};\n\n        let mut child = Command::new(\"sh\")\n            .arg(\"-c\")\n            .arg(command)\n            .stdin(Stdio::piped())\n            .stdout(Stdio::null())\n            .stderr(Stdio::null())\n            .spawn()\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to spawn hook: {command}\"))?;\n\n        if let Some(mut stdin) = child.stdin.take() {\n            // Best-effort write; ignore broken pipe if child exits early.\n            let _ = stdin.write_all(json.as_bytes());\n        }\n\n        // Wait for the child and check exit status.\n        let status = child\n            .wait()\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to wait for hook: {command}\"))?;\n\n        if !status.success() {\n            anyhow::bail!(\n                \"hook exited with status {}: {command}\",\n                status.code().unwrap_or(-1)\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// HTTP POST the event JSON to a webhook URL.\n    ///\n    /// Sets `Content-Type: application/json` and applies a 10-second timeout.\n    /// Returns an error if the request fails or the server returns a non-2xx\n    /// status. This runs inside the background writer task so blocking is\n    /// acceptable.\n    fn post_url(url: &str, json: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        ureq::post(url)\n            .set(\"Content-Type\", \"application/json\")\n            .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(10))\n            .send_string(json)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"webhook POST to {url} failed: {e}\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Sink for HookSink {\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n        let failures = self.dispatch(event);\n        for fail in &failures {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                hook_error = %fail.data,\n                original_event = %event.event_type,\n                \"telemetry hook dispatch failed\"\n            );\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn flush(&self, _deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {\n        // hooks run synchronously in accept(); nothing to drain\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Telemetry emitter ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Non-blocking telemetry emitter.\n///\n/// Cloning a `Telemetry` handle is cheap — it shares the same background\n/// writer and sequence counter.\n///\n/// The writer task must be started by calling `start()` from within a tokio\n/// runtime context. This is typically done at the beginning of `Worker::run()`.\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct Telemetry {\n    worker_id: WorkerId,\n    session_id: String,\n    sequence: Arc<AtomicU64>,\n    /// Workspace of the most recently claimed bead, shared by all telemetry handles.\n    current_workspace: Arc<std::sync::RwLock<Option<PathBuf>>>,\n    /// Wrapped in Arc<Mutex<Option<...>>> so that `shutdown()` can drop the\n    /// sender explicitly (closing the channel) even while clones still exist.\n    sender: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<mpsc::UnboundedSender<WriterMessage>>>>,\n    /// Pending writer state that needs to be spawned in an async context.\n    /// This is `Some` until `start()` is called.\n    pending_writer: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<PendingWriter>>>,\n    /// JoinHandle for the background writer thread, set by `start()`.\n    /// Uses std::thread::JoinHandle (not tokio::task::JoinHandle) because the\n    /// writer runs in its own dedicated thread with its own tokio runtime,\n    /// ensuring it can process messages before the main runtime's block_on().\n    writer_handle: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<std::thread::JoinHandle<()>>>>,\n    /// OTLP sink shutdown handle (feature-gated).\n    /// Stored separately so we can call its async shutdown method.\n    otlp_shutdown: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<OtlpShutdown>>>,\n}\n\n/// Worker identity used to populate OTLP resource attributes.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct TelemetryIdentity {\n    /// The configured worker agent or harness name.\n    pub agent: Option<String>,\n    /// The resolved model identifier, when the adapter declares one.\n    pub model: Option<String>,\n    /// The provider name (e.g., \"anthropic\", \"openai\").\n    pub provider: Option<String>,\n    /// The worker's workspace. OTLP sinks reduce this to its basename before export.\n    pub workspace: Option<PathBuf>,\n}\n\n/// Internal message type for the writer task.\n#[allow(clippy::large_enum_variant)]\nenum WriterMessage {\n    Event(TelemetryEvent),\n    Flush(tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<()>),\n}\n\n/// Holds the receiver and sinks until they can be spawned in an async context.\nstruct PendingWriter {\n    receiver: mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<WriterMessage>,\n    sinks: Vec<Box<dyn Sink>>,\n}\n\n/// Holds an OTLP sink for async shutdown (feature-gated).\nenum OtlpShutdown {\n    #[cfg(feature = \"otlp\")]\n    Sink(std::sync::Arc<crate::telemetry::OtlpSink>),\n    #[cfg(not(feature = \"otlp\"))]\n    None,\n}\n\nimpl OtlpShutdown {\n    /// Shutdown the OTLP sink gracefully.\n    ///\n    /// This drains all batched exports before returning.\n    #[cfg(feature = \"otlp\")]\n    async fn shutdown(self) -> Result<()> {\n        match self {\n            OtlpShutdown::Sink(sink) => {\n                // We need to extract the OtlpSink from Arc to call shutdown\n                // Try to unwrap the Arc - if there are other references, we'll force_flush instead\n                match std::sync::Arc::try_unwrap(sink) {\n                    Ok(otlp) => otlp.shutdown().await,\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\"Cannot shutdown OTLP sink: Arc has multiple references\");\n                        Ok(())\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// No-op shutdown when OTLP feature is disabled.\n    #[cfg(not(feature = \"otlp\"))]\n    async fn shutdown(self) -> Result<()> {\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Telemetry {\n    fn new_workspace_cell() -> Arc<std::sync::RwLock<Option<PathBuf>>> {\n        Arc::new(std::sync::RwLock::new(None))\n    }\n\n    /// Create a telemetry emitter that writes to a `FileSink`.\n    ///\n    /// Does not spawn any async tasks. Call [`start()`](Self::start) from\n    /// within a tokio runtime context before emitting events.\n    ///\n    /// Writes `worker.booting` directly to the file before returning, so even\n    /// if the writer thread fails to start, we have a trace in the JSONL log.\n    pub fn new(worker_id: WorkerId) -> Self {\n        let session_id = generate_session_id();\n        let (sender, receiver) = mpsc::unbounded_channel();\n\n        let mut sinks: Vec<Box<dyn Sink>> = Vec::new();\n        match FileSink::new(&worker_id, &session_id) {\n            Ok(s) => {\n                // Write boot event directly to file BEFORE spawning writer thread.\n                // Uses a 5-second timeout to prevent indefinite blocking on hung filesystems.\n                // This ensures we have a trace even if the writer thread fails to start.\n                let version = env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\");\n                if let Err(e) = s.write_boot_event_direct(&worker_id, &session_id, version) {\n                    // Check if this is a timeout error (filesystem may be hung)\n                    let error_msg = e.to_string();\n                    if error_msg.contains(\"timed out\")\n                        || error_msg.contains(\"filesystem may be hung\")\n                    {\n                        eprintln!(\n                            \"NEEDLE WARNING: boot event write timed out after 5s - filesystem may be hung or very slow\"\n                        );\n                        eprintln!(\"  Continuing without boot event in log file. Worker will still function.\");\n                        eprintln!(\n                            \"  Check: disk space, NFS mounts, filesystem latency, I/O errors\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                    tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"failed to write boot event directly to file\");\n                }\n                sinks.push(Box::new(s));\n            }\n            Err(e) => tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"failed to create telemetry file sink\"),\n        }\n\n        let sequence = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));\n        let pending = PendingWriter { receiver, sinks };\n\n        Telemetry {\n            worker_id,\n            session_id,\n            sequence,\n            current_workspace: Self::new_workspace_cell(),\n            sender: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(sender))),\n            pending_writer: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(pending))),\n            writer_handle: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),\n            otlp_shutdown: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a telemetry emitter with both file and stdout sinks.\n    ///\n    /// Does not spawn any async tasks. Worker will still function.\");\n                        eprintln!(\n                            \"  Check: disk space, NFS mounts, filesystem latency, I/O errors\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                    tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"failed to write boot event directly to file\");\n                }\n                sinks.push(Box::new(s));\n            }\n            Err(e) => tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"failed to create telemetry file sink\"),\n        }\n        if stdout_config.enabled {\n            sinks.push(Box::new(StdoutSink::new(stdout_config)));\n        }\n\n        let sequence = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));\n        let pending = PendingWriter { receiver, sinks };\n\n        Telemetry {\n            worker_id,\n            session_id,\n            sequence,\n            current_workspace: Self::new_workspace_cell(),\n            sender: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(sender))),\n            pending_writer: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(pending))),\n            writer_handle: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),\n            otlp_shutdown: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a telemetry emitter with file, stdout, and hook sinks.\n    ///\n    /// Does not spawn any async tasks.
