Non-blocking — returns immediately.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Err` only if the channel is disconnected (background task died).\n    pub fn emit(&self, kind: EventKind) -> Result<()> {\n        let event = self.make_event(&kind);\n        let seq = event.sequence;\n        tracing::debug!(event_type = %event.event_type, seq, \"telemetry event\");\n        // Use try_lock() to avoid blocking indefinitely if the telemetry writer\n        // is stuck holding the lock. If the lock is contended, we log and return\n        // Ok(()) to allow the worker to continue.\n        match self.sender.try_lock() {\n            Ok(guard) => {\n                if let Some(ref s) = *guard {\n                    s.send(WriterMessage::Event(event)).ok(); // ok() — never block, never panic\n                }\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    event_type = %event.event_type,\n                    seq,\n                    \"telemetry sender lock contended, skipping emit\"\n                );\n                Ok(())\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Emit an event without blocking — uses try_lock() instead of lock().\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Ok(())` if emitted successfully or if the lock is contended\n    /// (gracefully degrades). Returns `Err` only if the channel is disconnected.\n    ///\n    /// Use this in timeout recovery paths where blocking on emit() would\n    /// prevent the worker from recovering.\n    pub fn emit_try_lock(&self, kind: EventKind) -> Result<()> {\n        let event = self.make_event(&kind);\n        let seq = event.sequence;\n        // Use try_lock() to avoid blocking indefinitely if the telemetry writer\n        // is stuck holding the lock. If the lock is contended, we log and return\n        // Ok(()) to allow the worker to continue.\n        match self.sender.try_lock() {\n            Ok(guard) => {\n                if let Some(ref s) = *guard {\n                    s.send(WriterMessage::Event(event)).ok();\n                }\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    event_type = %event.event_type,\n                    seq,\n                    \"telemetry sender lock contended, skipping emit in timeout recovery path\"\n                );\n                Ok(())\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Force-flush all buffered events to disk (synchronous).\n    ///\n    /// Sends a flush request through the writer channel and waits (up to\n    /// `timeout`) for the writer task to flush its BufWriter. Used after\n    /// `worker.booting` so the event is visible on disk even if subsequent\n    /// init steps block.\n    ///\n    /// NOTE: This uses `blocking_recv()` and must be called from outside a\n    /// tokio runtime (e.g., in `run_worker` before `rt.block_on`). Use\n    /// `force_flush_async()` from within async contexts.\n    pub fn force_flush(&self, timeout: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {\n        let (tx, rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel();\n        // Use try_lock() to avoid blocking indefinitely if the telemetry writer\n        // is stuck holding the lock.\n        match self.sender.try_lock() {\n            Ok(guard) => {\n                if let Some(ref s) = *guard {\n                    s.send(WriterMessage::Flush(tx)).ok();\n                }\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\"telemetry sender lock contended in force_flush, skipping flush\");\n                return Ok(()); // Don't fail — the writer will eventually flush\n            }\n        }\n        // Block until the writer task flushes or timeout.\n        // Spawn a thread to handle the blocking recv with a timeout.\n        let handle = std::thread::spawn(move || rx.blocking_recv());\n        let start = std::time::Instant::now();\n        loop {\n            if handle.is_finished() {\n                return Ok(());\n            }\n            if start.elapsed() >= timeout {\n                tracing::warn!(\"force_flush timed out after {:?}\", timeout);\n                return Ok(()); // Don't fail — the writer will eventually flush\n            }\n            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(50));\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Force-flush all buffered events to disk (async).\n    ///\n    /// Async version of `force_flush()` that can be called from within a\n    /// tokio runtime. Use this in `Worker::run()` and other async contexts.\n    pub async fn force_flush_async(&self, timeout: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {\n        let (tx, rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel();\n        // Use try_lock() to avoid blocking indefinitely if the telemetry writer\n        // is stuck holding the lock.\n        match self.sender.try_lock() {\n            Ok(guard) => {\n                if let Some(ref s) = *guard {\n                    s.send(WriterMessage::Flush(tx)).ok();\n                }\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    \"telemetry sender lock contended in force_flush_async, skipping flush\"\n                );\n                return Ok(()); // Don't fail — the writer will eventually flush\n            }\n        }\n        // Wait for the writer task to flush, with timeout.\n        match tokio::time::timeout(timeout, rx).await {\n            Ok(Ok(())) => Ok(()),\n            Ok(Err(_)) => Ok(()), // Channel closed, writer already flushed\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\"force_flush_async timed out after {:?}\", timeout);\n                Ok(())\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Emit an event synchronously, writing directly to the file sink.\n    ///\n    /// This bypasses the async channel and writes immediately to the file.\n    /// Use this for critical early-boot events (like `worker.booting`) that\n    /// must be visible even if the async writer hasn't started yet.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Err` if the pending writer is not available (already started)\n    /// or if writing to the file fails.\n    pub fn emit_sync(&self, kind: EventKind) -> Result<()> {\n        let event = self.make_event(&kind);\n\n        // Take the pending writer temporarily to write directly to sinks.\n        let pending_guard = self.pending_writer.lock().unwrap();\n        if let Some(ref pending) = *pending_guard {\n            // Write directly to each sink (typically just FileSink).\n            for sink in &pending.sinks {\n                if let Err(e) = sink.accept(&event) {\n                    tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"sync emit to sink failed\");\n                }\n            }\n            Ok(())\n        } else {\n            // Pending writer already consumed by start().\n            Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"cannot emit_sync after start()\"))\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Return a reference to the session ID for log path discovery.\n    pub fn session_id(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.session_id\n    }\n\n    /// Return a reference to the worker ID.\n    pub fn worker_id(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.worker_id\n    }\n\n    /// Create a telemetry emitter writing to a specific log directory.\n    ///\n    /// Use this when the config specifies a custom log path. Does not spawn\n    /// any async tasks. Call [`start()`](Self::start) from within a tokio\n    /// runtime context before emitting events.\n    pub fn with_log_dir(worker_id: WorkerId, log_dir: &Path) -> Self {\n        let session_id = generate_session_id();\n        let (sender, receiver) = mpsc::unbounded_channel();\n\n        let mut sinks: Vec<Box<dyn Sink>> = Vec::new();\n        match FileSink::with_dir(log_dir.to_path_buf(), &worker_id, &session_id) {\n            Ok(s) => sinks.push(Box::new(s)),\n            Err(e) => tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"failed to create telemetry file sink\"),\n        }\n\n        let sequence = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));\n        let pending = PendingWriter { receiver, sinks };\n\n        Telemetry {\n            worker_id,\n            session_id,\n            sequence,\n            current_workspace: Self::new_workspace_cell(),\n            sender: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(sender))),\n            pending_writer: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(pending))),\n            writer_handle: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),\n            otlp_shutdown: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Start the background writer task.\n    ///\n    /// Must be called from within a tokio runtime context (e.g. inside\n    /// `block_on` or an async function). Calling this more than once on\n    /// the same handle is a no-op.\n    pub fn start(&self) {\n        let pending = self.pending_writer.lock().unwrap().take();\n        if let Some(pw) = pending {\n            let handle = Self::spawn_writer(pw.receiver, pw.sinks, None);\n            *self.writer_handle.lock().unwrap() = Some(handle);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Start the background writer task and wait for it to be ready.\n    ///\n    /// Returns a Future that completes when the writer thread has started\n    /// and is ready to process events. Use this instead of `start()` when\n    /// you need to guarantee that events emitted immediately after will\n    /// be processed (e.g., for `worker.booting` as the first JSONL event).\n    ///\n    /// Must be called from within a tokio runtime context.\n    pub async fn start_and_wait(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        eprintln!(\"NEEDLE telemetry: starting writer thread and waiting for ready signal...\");\n        let pending = self.pending_writer.lock().unwrap().take();\n        if let Some(pw) = pending {\n            let (ready_tx, ready_rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel();\n            let handle = Self::spawn_writer(pw.receiver, pw.sinks, Some(ready_tx));\n            *self.writer_handle.lock().unwrap() = Some(handle);\n\n            // Wait for the writer thread to signal it's ready.\n            // Use a timeout to avoid hanging if the thread fails to start.\n            eprintln!(\"NEEDLE telemetry: waiting for writer thread ready signal (timeout 5s)...\");\n            tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5), ready_rx)\n                .await\n                .map_err(|_| anyhow::anyhow!(\"writer thread failed to start within 5s\"))?\n                .map_err(|_| anyhow::anyhow!(\"writer thread closed before signaling ready\"))?;\n            eprintln!(\"NEEDLE telemetry: writer thread ready signal received\");\n        } else {\n            eprintln!(\"NEEDLE telemetry: writer thread already started, skipping\");\n        }\n        eprintln!(\"NEEDLE telemetry: start_and_wait complete\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Flush and shut down the background writer.\n    ///\n    /// Drops the shared sender (closing the channel) so the writer thread\n    /// processes all buffered events and flushes its `BufWriter` before\n    /// exiting. Joins the thread to guarantee completion.\n    ///\n    /// Call this at every terminal path in the worker before the tokio\n    /// Runtime is dropped, or the BufWriter flush will be cancelled.\n    pub async fn shutdown(&self) {\n        // Drop the sender to signal EOF to the writer thread.\n        *self.sender.lock().unwrap() = None;\n        // Join the writer thread so the flush completes before we return.\n        let handle = self.writer_handle.lock().unwrap().take();\n        if let Some(h) = handle {\n            let _ = h.join();\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Shut down the OTLP sink gracefully (if enabled).\n    ///\n    /// This drains all batched OTLP exports before returning. Should be called\n    /// once at process exit, before the Tokio runtime is dropped.\n    ///\n    /// This is a no-op if the OTLP sink is not configured or if the `otlp`\n    /// feature is disabled.\n    pub async fn shutdown_otlp(&self) {\n        let shutdown = self.otlp_shutdown.lock().unwrap().take();\n        if let Some(s) = shutdown {\n            if let Err(e) = s.shutdown().await {\n                tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"OTLP shutdown failed\");\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Record the current queue depth for the `needle.queue.depth` observable gauge.\n    ///\n    /// This updates the per-priority counts that the observable gauge callback reads.\n    /// The queue depth should be sampled during strand evaluation (typically after\n    /// the Pluck strand returns candidates).\n    ///\n    /// The `depths` parameter maps priority level -> bead count at that priority.\n    ///\n    /// This is a no-op if the OTLP sink is not configured or if the `otlp`\n    /// feature is disabled.\n    pub fn record_queue_depth(&self, depths: std::collections::HashMap<u8, u64>) {\n        #[cfg(feature = \"otlp\")]\n        {\n            let shutdown = self.otlp_shutdown.lock().unwrap();\n            if let Some(OtlpShutdown::Sink(sink)) = &*shutdown {\n                sink.record_queue_depth(depths);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Spawn background writer task draining the channel to all registered sinks.\n    ///\n    /// Spawns a dedicated thread with its own tokio runtime so the writer task\n    /// can immediately start processing messages, even before the main runtime's\n    /// `block_on()` is called. This fixes a deadlock where `force_flush()` would\n    /// wait indefinitely for a response from a task that hasn't started yet.\n    ///\n    /// If `ready_signal` is provided, sends () through it when the writer is\n    /// ready to process events.\n    fn spawn_writer(\n        receiver: mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<WriterMessage>,\n        sinks: Vec<Box<dyn Sink>>,\n        ready_signal: Option<tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<()>>,\n    ) -> std::thread::JoinHandle<()> {\n        std::thread::spawn(move || {\n            let rt = match tokio::runtime::Runtime::new() {\n                Ok(r) => r,\n                Err(e) => {\n                    // Fallback to stderr when tracing may not be initialized yet\n                    eprintln!(\n                        \"NEEDLE telemetry writer thread: FAILED to create tokio runtime: {}\",\n                        e\n                    );\n                    tracing::error!(error = %e, \"failed to create writer runtime\");\n                    // Signal that we failed (by dropping the sender without sending)\n                    drop(ready_signal);\n                    return;\n                }\n            };\n            eprintln!(\"NEEDLE telemetry writer thread: started successfully\");\n            if sinks.is_empty() {\n                eprintln!(\"NEEDLE telemetry writer thread: WARNING - no sinks configured, events will be discarded!\");\n            }\n            let mut receiver = receiver;\n            rt.block_on(async move {\n                // Signal that the writer is ready to process events.\n                // Do this before entering the recv() loop so the caller\n                // can proceed as soon as we're ready.\n                eprintln!(\"NEEDLE telemetry writer thread: signaling ready to main thread...\");\n                if let Some(tx) = ready_signal {\n                    tx.send(()).ok();\n                }\n                eprintln!(\"NEEDLE telemetry writer thread: ready, waiting for events...\");\n\n                let deadline = std::time::Duration::from_secs(5);\n                let mut event_count = 0u64;\n                while let Some(msg) = receiver.recv().await {\n                    match msg {\n                        WriterMessage::Event(event) => {\n                            event_count += 1;\n                            for sink in &sinks {\n                                if let Err(e) = sink.accept(&event) {\n                                    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE telemetry: sink accept failed for event {}: {}\", event.event_type, e);\n                                    tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"telemetry sink accept failed\");\n                                }\n                            }\n                            if event_count == 1 {\n                                eprintln!(\"NEEDLE telemetry writer thread: first event written: {}\", event.event_type);\n                            }\n                        }\n                        WriterMessage::Flush(reply) => {\n                            for sink in &sinks {\n                                if let Err(e) = sink.flush(deadline) {\n                                    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE telemetry: sink flush failed: {:#}\", e);\n                                    tracing::warn!(error = ?e, \"telemetry sink flush on demand failed\");\n                                }\n                            }\n                            reply.send(()).ok();\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n                for sink in &sinks {\n                    if let Err(e) = sink.flush(deadline) {\n                        tracing::warn!(error = ?e, \"telemetry sink flush failed\");\n                    }\n                }\n            })\n        })\n    }\n\n    // ─── Structured logging helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Emit a structured log event.\n    ///\n    /// This is a convenience method for logging with explicit phase, level, and context.\n    /// The event is emitted through the telemetry system as a `log.entry` event.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `phase` - The phase identifier (e.g., \"dispatch\", \"claim\", \"outcome\")\n    /// * `level` - Log level (e.g., \"info\", \"warn\", \"error\", \"debug\")\n    /// * `context` - Structured context data as a JSON value\n    /// * `bead_id` - Optional bead context when relevant\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    ///\n    /// ```no_run\n    /// use needle::telemetry::Telemetry;\n    /// use serde_json::json;\n    ///\n    /// # let telemetry: Telemetry = unimplemented!();\n    /// telemetry.log(\n    ///     \"dispatch\",\n    ///     \"info\",\n    ///     json!({ \"agent\": \"claude\", \"prompt_length\": 1234 }),\n    ///     Some(\"needle-123\".into()),\n    /// ).ok();\n    /// ```\n    pub fn log(\n        &self,\n        phase: impl Into<String>,\n        level: impl Into<String>,\n        context: serde_json::Value,\n        bead_id: Option<BeadId>,\n    ) -> Result<()> {\n        self.emit(EventKind::Log {\n            phase: phase.into(),\n            level: level.into(),\n            context,\n            bead_id,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Emit an info-level log event.\n    ///\n    /// Convenience method for logging at \"info\" level.\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    ///\n    /// ```no_run\n    /// # use needle::telemetry::Telemetry;\n    /// # use serde_json::json;\n    /// # let telemetry: Telemetry = unimplemented!();\n    /// telemetry.log_info(\"dispatch\", json!({ \"status\": \"started\" })).ok();\n    /// ```\n    pub fn log_info(&self, phase: impl Into<String>, context: serde_json::Value) -> Result<()> {\n        self.log(phase, \"info\", context, None)\n    }\n\n    /// Emit an info-level log event with bead context.\n    ///\n    /// Convenience method for logging at \"info\" level with bead association.\n    pub fn log_info_with_bead(\n        &self,\n        phase: impl Into<String>,\n        context: serde_json::Value,\n        bead_id: &BeadId,\n    ) -> Result<()> {\n        self.log(phase, \"info\", context, Some(bead_id.clone()))\n    }\n\n    /// Emit a warn-level log event.\n    ///\n    /// Convenience method for logging at \"warn\" level.\n    pub fn log_warn(&self, phase: impl Into<String>, context: serde_json::Value) -> Result<()> {\n        self.log(phase, \"warn\", context, None)\n    }\n\n    /// Emit a warn-level log event with bead context.\n    ///\n    /// Convenience method for logging at \"warn\" level with bead association.\n    pub fn log_warn_with_bead(\n        &self,\n        phase: impl Into<String>,\n        context: serde_json::Value,\n        bead_id: &BeadId,\n    ) -> Result<()> {\n        self.log(phase, \"warn\", context, Some(bead_id.clone()))\n    }\n\n    /// Emit an error-level log event.\n    ///\n    /// Convenience method for logging at \"error\" level.\n    pub fn log_error(&self, phase: impl Into<String>, context: serde_json::Value) -> Result<()> {\n        self.log(phase, \"error\", context, None)\n    }\n\n    /// Emit an error-level log event with bead context.\n    ///\n    /// Convenience method for logging at \"error\" level with bead association.\n    pub fn log_error_with_bead(\n        &self,\n        phase: impl Into<String>,\n        context: serde_json::Value,\n        bead_id: &BeadId,\n    ) -> Result<()> {\n        self.log(phase, \"error\", context, Some(bead_id.clone()))\n    }\n\n    /// Emit a debug-level log event.\n    ///\n    /// Convenience method for logging at \"debug\" level.\n    pub fn log_debug(&self, phase: impl Into<String>, context: serde_json::Value) -> Result<()> {\n        self.log(phase, \"debug\", context, None)\n    }\n\n    /// Emit a debug-level log event with bead context.\n    ///\n    /// Convenience method for logging at \"debug\" level with bead association.\n    pub fn log_debug_with_bead(\n        &self,\n        phase: impl Into<String>,\n        context: serde_json::Value,\n        bead_id: &BeadId,\n    ) -> Result<()> {\n        self.log(phase, \"debug\", context, Some(bead_id.clone()))\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Log querying ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Parse a `--since` value into a `DateTime<Utc>`.\n///\n/// Accepts relative durations like `1h`, `30m`, `24h`, `7d` or absolute\n/// ISO 8601 / date strings like `2026-03-20` or `2026-03-20T15:00:00Z`.\npub fn parse_since(input: &str) -> Result<DateTime<Utc>> {\n    let trimmed = input.trim();\n\n    // Try relative duration: Nh, Nm, Nd, Ns\n    if let Some(rest) = trimmed.strip_suffix('h') {\n        let hours: i64 = rest.parse().context(\"invalid hours in --since\")?;\n        return Ok(Utc::now() - chrono::Duration::hours(hours));\n    }\n    if let Some(rest) = trimmed.strip_suffix('m') {\n        let mins: i64 = rest.parse().context(\"invalid minutes in --since\")?;\n        return Ok(Utc::now() - chrono::Duration::minutes(mins));\n    }\n    if let Some(rest) = trimmed.strip_suffix('d') {\n        let days: i64 = rest.parse().context(\"invalid days in --since\")?;\n        return Ok(Utc::now() - chrono::Duration::days(days));\n    }\n    if let Some(rest) = trimmed.strip_suffix('s') {\n        if rest.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) {\n            let secs: i64 = rest.parse().context(\"invalid seconds in --since\")?;\n            return Ok(Utc::now() - chrono::Duration::seconds(secs));\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Try ISO 8601 with time\n    if let Ok(dt) = trimmed.parse::<DateTime<Utc>>() {\n        return Ok(dt);\n    }\n\n    // Try date-only (YYYY-MM-DD) → midnight UTC\n    if let Ok(date) = chrono::NaiveDate::parse_from_str(trimmed, \"%Y-%m-%d\") {\n        let dt = date.and_hms_opt(0, 0, 0).context(\"invalid date\")?;\n        return Ok(DateTime::from_naive_utc_and_offset(dt, Utc));\n    }\n\n    anyhow::bail!(\n        \"unrecognized --since format: '{}'. Use relative (1h, 30m, 7d) or ISO date (2026-03-20)\",\n        input\n    )\n}\n\n/// Convert a glob-style filter pattern to a regex.\n///\n/// Supports `*` as wildcard. E.g., `bead.claim.*` → `^bead\\.claim\\..*$`\npub fn glob_to_regex(pattern: &str) -> Result<regex::Regex> {\n    let mut re = String::from(\"^\");\n    for ch in pattern.chars() {\n        match ch {\n            '*' => re.push_str(\".*\"),\n            '.' => re.push_str(\"\\\\.\"),\n            '?' => re.push('.'),\n            c => re.push(c),\n        }\n    }\n    re.push('$');\n    regex::Regex::new(&re).context(\"invalid filter pattern\")\n}\n\n// ─── Rich filter expressions ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A single filter predicate applied to a telemetry event.\nenum FilterPredicate {\n    /// Glob pattern matched against `event_type` (backward-compatible).\n    EventTypeGlob(regex::Regex),\n    /// Exact case-sensitive match on a named field.\n    FieldEquals { field: String, value: String },\n    /// Regex match on a named field.\n    FieldRegex {\n        field: String,\n        pattern: regex::Regex,\n    },\n    /// Numeric greater-than on a named field.\n    FieldGt { field: String, threshold: f64 },\n}\n\n/// A conjunction (AND) of filter predicates for querying telemetry events.\n///\n/// Build from one or more expression strings with [`LogsFilter::parse`].\npub struct LogsFilter {\n    predicates: Vec<FilterPredicate>,\n}\n\nimpl LogsFilter {\n    /// Parse a list of filter expression strings into a `LogsFilter`.\n    ///\n    /// Each expression may be one of:\n    /// - `field=value`   — exact string match\n    /// - `field~pattern` — regex match\n    /// - `field>number`  — numeric greater-than\n    /// - `glob`          — glob pattern on `event_type` (no operator, backward compat)\n    ///\n    /// All predicates are ANDed together.\n    pub fn parse(exprs: &[&str]) -> Result<Self> {\n        let mut predicates = Vec::with_capacity(exprs.len());\n        for expr in exprs {\n            let expr = expr.trim();\n            if let Some(pos) = expr.find('=') {\n                let field = expr[..pos].to_string();\n                let value = expr[pos + 1..].to_string();\n                predicates.push(FilterPredicate::FieldEquals { field, value });\n            } else if let Some(pos) = expr.find('~') {\n                let field = expr[..pos].to_string();\n                let raw = &expr[pos + 1..];\n                let pattern = regex::Regex::new(raw)\n                    .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid regex in filter '{expr}': {raw}\"))?;\n                predicates.push(FilterPredicate::FieldRegex { field, pattern });\n            } else if let Some(pos) = expr.find('>') {\n                let field = expr[..pos].to_string();\n                let raw = &expr[pos + 1..];\n                let threshold: f64 = raw\n                    .parse()\n                    .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid number in filter '{expr}': {raw}\"))?;\n                predicates.push(FilterPredicate::FieldGt { field, threshold });\n            } else {\n                // Treat as glob pattern on event_type.\n                let re = glob_to_regex(expr)?;\n                predicates.push(FilterPredicate::EventTypeGlob(re));\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(LogsFilter { predicates })\n    }\n\n    /// Return `true` if the event satisfies all predicates.\n    pub fn matches(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> bool {\n        self.predicates.iter().all(|p| predicate_matches(p, event))\n    }\n\n    /// Return `true` if the filter has no predicates (matches everything).\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.predicates.is_empty()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Evaluate a single predicate against an event.\nfn predicate_matches(pred: &FilterPredicate, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> bool {\n    match pred {\n        FilterPredicate::EventTypeGlob(re) => re.is_match(&event.event_type),\n        FilterPredicate::FieldEquals { field, value } => {\n            get_event_field_str(event, field).as_deref() == Some(value.as_str())\n        }\n        FilterPredicate::FieldRegex { field, pattern } => get_event_field_str(event, field)\n            .map(|v| pattern.is_match(&v))\n            .unwrap_or(false),\n        FilterPredicate::FieldGt { field, threshold } => get_event_field_f64(event, field)\n            .map(|v| v > *threshold)\n            .unwrap_or(false),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Extract a named field from a `TelemetryEvent` as a string.\n///\n/// Supported top-level fields: `event_type`, `worker_id`, `session_id`,\n/// `bead_id`, `workspace`. Data sub-fields can be accessed directly by\n/// name (matched against `event.data[field]`).\nfn get_event_field_str(event: &TelemetryEvent, field: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    match field {\n        \"event_type\" => Some(event.event_type.clone()),\n        \"worker_id\" => Some(event.worker_id.clone()),\n        \"session_id\" => Some(event.session_id.clone()),\n        \"bead_id\" => event.bead_id.as_ref().map(|b| b.as_ref().to_string()),\n        \"workspace\" => event.workspace.as_ref().map(|p| p.display().to_string()),\n        _ => {\n            // Check data sub-fields.\n            event.data.get(field).map(|v| match v {\n                serde_json::Value::String(s) => s.clone(),\n                other => other.to_string(),\n            })\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Extract a named field from a `TelemetryEvent` as a float.\n///\n/// Supported numeric fields: `duration_ms`, `sequence`, and any numeric key\n/// in `event.data`.\nfn get_event_field_f64(event: &TelemetryEvent, field: &str) -> Option<f64> {\n    match field {\n        \"duration_ms\" => event.duration_ms.map(|d| d as f64),\n        \"sequence\" => Some(event.sequence as f64),\n        _ => event.data.get(field).and_then(|v| v.as_f64()),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Parse a time-bound string (relative or absolute) into a UTC timestamp.\n///\n/// This is an alias for [`parse_since`] and accepts the same formats.\npub fn parse_until(input: &str) -> Result<DateTime<Utc>> {\n    parse_since(input)\n}\n\n/// Read and parse JSONL log files from a directory.\n///\n/// Returns events sorted by timestamp. Optionally filters by `since`, `until`,\n/// and a [`LogsFilter`] predicate set.\npub fn read_logs(\n    log_dir: &Path,\n    since: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,\n    until: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,\n    filter: Option<&LogsFilter>,\n) -> Result<Vec<TelemetryEvent>> {\n    let mut events = Vec::new();\n\n    if !log_dir.is_dir() {\n        return Ok(events);\n    }\n\n    let entries = std::fs::read_dir(log_dir)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"cannot read log directory: {}\", log_dir.display()))?;\n\n    for entry in entries {\n        let entry = entry?;\n        let path = entry.path();\n        if path.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()) != Some(\"jsonl\") {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let contents = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"cannot read log file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        for line in contents.lines() {\n            if line.trim().is_empty() {\n                continue;\n            }\n            let event: TelemetryEvent = match serde_json::from_str(line) {\n                Ok(e) => e,\n                Err(_) => continue, // Skip malformed lines\n            };\n            if let Some(ref cutoff) = since {\n                if event.timestamp < *cutoff {\n                    continue;\n                }\n            }\n            if let Some(ref ceiling) = until {\n                if event.timestamp > *ceiling {\n                    continue;\n                }\n            }\n            if let Some(f) = filter {\n                if !f.matches(&event) {\n                    continue;\n                }\n            }\n            events.push(event);\n        }\n    }\n\n    events.sort_by_key(|a| a.timestamp);\n    Ok(events)\n}\n\n/// Compute cost summary from effort events.\npub fn compute_cost_summary(events: &[TelemetryEvent]) -> CostSummary {\n    let mut summary = CostSummary::default();\n    for event in events {\n        if event.event_type == \"effort.recorded\" {\n            summary.total_events += 1;\n            if let Some(cost) = event.data[\"estimated_cost_usd\"].as_f64() {\n                summary.total_cost_usd += cost;\n            }\n            if let Some(tokens_in) = event.data[\"tokens_in\"].as_u64() {\n                summary.total_tokens_in += tokens_in;\n            }\n            if let Some(tokens_out) = event.data[\"tokens_out\"].as_u64() {\n                summary.total_tokens_out += tokens_out;\n            }\n            if let Some(elapsed) = event.data[\"elapsed_ms\"].as_u64() {\n                summary.total_elapsed_ms += elapsed;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    summary\n}\n\n/// Aggregated cost data from effort events.\n#[derive(Debug, Default)]\npub struct CostSummary {\n    pub total_events: u64,\n    pub total_cost_usd: f64,\n    pub total_tokens_in: u64,\n    pub total_tokens_out: u64,\n    pub total_elapsed_ms: u64,\n}\n\n/// Per-worker cost breakdown from effort events.\n#[derive(Debug, Default)]\npub struct WorkerCostSummary {\n    pub worker_id: String,\n    pub total_events: u64,\n    pub total_cost_usd: f64,\n    pub total_tokens_in: u64,\n    pub total_tokens_out: u64,\n    pub total_elapsed_ms: u64,\n}\n\n/// Compute per-worker cost breakdown from effort events.\n///\n/// Returns one entry per worker that has at least one effort event, sorted\n/// by descending total cost.\npub fn compute_cost_by_worker(events: &[TelemetryEvent]) -> Vec<WorkerCostSummary> {\n    let mut map: std::collections::HashMap<String, WorkerCostSummary> =\n        std::collections::HashMap::new();\n    for event in events {\n        if event.event_type != \"effort.recorded\" {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let entry = map\n            .entry(event.worker_id.clone())\n            .or_insert_with(|| WorkerCostSummary {\n                worker_id: event.worker_id.clone(),\n                ..Default::default()\n            });\n        entry.total_events += 1;\n        if let Some(cost) = event.data[\"estimated_cost_usd\"].as_f64() {\n            entry.total_cost_usd += cost;\n        }\n        if let Some(tokens_in) = event.data[\"tokens_in\"].as_u64() {\n            entry.total_tokens_in += tokens_in;\n        }\n        if let Some(tokens_out) = event.data[\"tokens_out\"].as_u64() {\n            entry.total_tokens_out += tokens_out;\n        }\n        if let Some(elapsed) = event.data[\"elapsed_ms\"].as_u64() {\n            entry.total_elapsed_ms += elapsed;\n        }\n    }\n    let mut result: Vec<WorkerCostSummary> = map.into_values().collect();\n    result.sort_by(|a, b| {\n        b.total_cost_usd\n            .partial_cmp(&a.total_cost_usd)\n            .unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal)\n    });\n    result\n}\n\n/// Per-workspace cost breakdown from effort events.\n#[derive(Debug, Default)]\npub struct WorkspaceCostSummary {\n    pub workspace: String,\n    pub total_events: u64,\n    pub total_cost_usd: f64,\n    pub total_tokens_in: u64,\n    pub total_tokens_out: u64,\n    pub total_elapsed_ms: u64,\n}\n\n/// Compute per-workspace cost breakdown from effort events.\n///\n/// Returns one entry per workspace that has at least one effort event, sorted\n/// by descending total cost.\npub fn compute_cost_by_workspace(events: &[TelemetryEvent]) -> Vec<WorkspaceCostSummary> {\n    let mut map: std::collections::HashMap<String, WorkspaceCostSummary> =\n        std::collections::HashMap::new();\n    for event in events {\n        if event.event_type != \"effort.recorded\" {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let ws_key = event\n            .workspace\n            .as_ref()\n            .map(|p| p.display().to_string())\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| \"unknown\".to_string());\n        let entry = map\n            .entry(ws_key.clone())\n            .or_insert_with(|| WorkspaceCostSummary {\n                workspace: ws_key,\n                ..Default::default()\n            });\n        entry.total_events += 1;\n        if let Some(cost) = event.data[\"estimated_cost_usd\"].as_f64() {\n            entry.total_cost_usd += cost;\n        }\n        if let Some(tokens_in) = event.data[\"tokens_in\"].as_u64() {\n            entry.total_tokens_in += tokens_in;\n        }\n        if let Some(tokens_out) = event.data[\"tokens_out\"].as_u64() {\n            entry.total_tokens_out += tokens_out;\n        }\n        if let Some(elapsed) = event.data[\"elapsed_ms\"].as_u64() {\n            entry.total_elapsed_ms += elapsed;\n        }\n    }\n    let mut result: Vec<WorkspaceCostSummary> = map.into_values().collect();\n    result.sort_by(|a, b| {\n        b.total_cost_usd\n            .partial_cmp(&a.total_cost_usd)\n            .unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal)\n    });\n    result\n}\n\n// ─── Structured logging macros ─────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Emit a structured log event with the specified level.\n///\n/// This macro provides a convenient way to log structured events with the\n/// telemetry system. It automatically serializes the context to JSON and\n/// emits it through the provided telemetry instance.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `$telemetry` - The telemetry instance to emit through\n/// * `$level` - Log level: \"info\", \"warn\", \"error\", or \"debug\"\n/// * `$phase` - Phase identifier (e.g., \"dispatch\", \"claim\")\n/// * `$context` - JSON object with context data\n/// * `$bead_id` - Optional bead ID\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// # use needle::telemetry::Telemetry;\n/// # use needle::log;\n/// # use needle::types::BeadId;\n/// # let telemetry: Telemetry = unimplemented!();\n/// // Basic info log\n/// log!(telemetry, \"info\", \"dispatch\", {\"status\": \"started\"});\n///\n/// // Log with bead context\n/// let bead_id = BeadId::from(\"needle-123\");\n/// log!(telemetry, \"info\", \"claim\", {\"attempt\": 1}, Some(bead_id));\n///\n/// // Error log with context\n/// log!(telemetry, \"error\", \"outcome\", {\n///     \"exit_code\": 1,\n///     \"reason\": \"timeout\"\n/// }, None::<BeadId>);\n/// ```\n#[macro_export]\nmacro_rules! log {\n    ($telemetry:expr, $level:expr, $phase:expr, {$($key:ident: $value:expr),* $(,)?}) => {\n        $telemetry.log(\n            $phase,\n            $level,\n            $crate::serde_json::json!({ $($key: $value),* }),\n            None,\n        )\n    };\n    ($telemetry:expr, $level:expr, $phase:expr, {$($key:ident: $value:expr),* $(,)?}, $bead_id:expr) => {\n        $telemetry.log(\n            $phase,\n            $level,\n            $crate::serde_json::json!({ $($key: $value),* }),\n            $bead_id,\n        )\n    };\n}\n\n/// Emit an info-level structured log event.\n///\n/// Convenience macro for logging at \"info\" level.\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// # use needle::telemetry::Telemetry;\n/// # use needle::log_info;\n/// # let telemetry: Telemetry = unimplemented!();\n/// log_info!(telemetry, \"dispatch\", {\"status\": \"started\", \"agent\": \"claude\"});\n/// ```\n#[macro_export]\nmacro_rules! log_info {\n    ($telemetry:expr, $phase:expr, {$($key:ident: $value:expr),* $(,)?}) => {\n        $telemetry.log_info($phase, $crate::serde_json::json!({ $($key: $value),* }))\n    };\n    ($telemetry:expr, $phase:expr, {$($key:ident: $value:expr),* $(,)?}, $bead_id:expr) => {\n        $telemetry.log_info_with_bead($phase, $crate::serde_json::json!({ $($key: $value),* }), &$bead_id)\n    };\n}\n\n/// Emit a warn-level structured log event.\n///\n/// Convenience macro for logging at \"warn\" level.\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// # use needle::telemetry::Telemetry;\n/// # use needle::log_warn;\n/// # let telemetry: Telemetry = unimplemented!();\n/// log_warn!(telemetry, \"claim\", {\"reason\": \"race_lost\", \"attempts\": 3});\n/// ```\n#[macro_export]\nmacro_rules! log_warn {\n    ($telemetry:expr, $phase:expr, {$($key:ident: $value:expr),* $(,)?}) => {\n        $telemetry.log_warn($phase, $crate::serde_json::json!({ $($key: $value),* }))\n    };\n    ($telemetry:expr, $phase:expr, {$($key:ident: $value:expr),* $(,)?}, $bead_id:expr) => {\n        $telemetry.log_warn_with_bead($phase, $crate::serde_json::json!({ $($key: $value),* }), &$bead_id)\n    };\n}\n\n/// Emit an error-level structured log event.\n///\n/// Convenience macro for logging at \"error\" level.\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// # use needle::telemetry::Telemetry;\n/// # use needle::log_error;\n/// # let telemetry: Telemetry = unimplemented!();\n/// log_error!(telemetry, \"outcome\", {\"exit_code\": 1, \"error\": \"timeout\"});\n/// ```\n#[macro_export]\nmacro_rules! log_error {\n    ($telemetry:expr, $phase:expr, {$($key:ident: $value:expr),* $(,)?}) => {\n        $telemetry.log_error($phase, $crate::serde_json::json!({ $($key: $value),* }))\n    };\n    ($telemetry:expr, $phase:expr, {$($key:ident: $value:expr),* $(,)?}, $bead_id:expr) => {\n        $telemetry.log_error_with_bead($phase, $crate::serde_json::json!({ $($key: $value),* }), &$bead_id)\n    };\n}\n\n/// Emit a debug-level structured log event.\n///\n/// Convenience macro for logging at \"debug\" level.\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// # use needle::telemetry::Telemetry;\n/// # use needle::log_debug;\n/// # let telemetry: Telemetry = unimplemented!();\n/// log_debug!(telemetry, \"routing\", {\"model\": \"sonnet-4\", \"confidence\": 0.95});\n/// ```\n#[macro_export]\nmacro_rules! log_debug {\n    ($telemetry:expr, $phase:expr, {$($key:ident: $value:expr),* $(,)?}) => {\n        $telemetry.log_debug($phase, $crate::serde_json::json!({ $($key: $value),* }))\n    };\n    ($telemetry:expr, $phase:expr, {$($key:ident: $value:expr),* $(,)?}, $bead_id:expr) => {\n        $telemetry.log_debug_with_bead($phase, $crate::serde_json::json!({ $($key: $value),* }), &$bead_id)\n    };\n}\n\n// ─── Unit tests the channel) and *await* the\n    /// writer task's JoinHandle so the flush runs before the tokio Runtime drops.\n    #[tokio::test]\n    async fn shutdown_flushes_bufwriter_on_short_lived_session() {\n        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(\"needle-test-shutdown-flush\");\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);\n\n        let (telemetry, path) = telemetry.start();\n\n        // Emit a handful of small events — total << 8 KB BufWriter threshold.\n        telemetry\n            .emit(EventKind::WorkerStarted {\n                worker_name: \"test-worker\".to_string(),\n                version: \"0.1.0\".to_string(),\n            })\n            .unwrap();\n        telemetry.emit(EventKind::QueueEmpty).unwrap();\n        telemetry\n            .emit(EventKind::WorkerStopped {\n                reason: \"exhausted\".to_string(),\n                beads_processed: 0,\n                uptime_secs: 0,\n            })\n            .unwrap();\n\n        // shutdown() closes the channel, awaits the writer task, and guarantees\n        // the BufWriter is flushed before returning — no sleep required.\n        telemetry.shutdown().await;\n\n        // The file must contain the 4 events (worker.booting is written during init,\n        // plus the 3 events emitted by the test). std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);\n    }\n\n    /// Verify that events emitted inside an OTel span carry the correct\n    /// trace_id and span_id in 32/16 lowercase-hex W3C format.\n    #[cfg(feature =      }\n        impl Sink for DeadlineSink {\n            fn accept(&self, _: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            fn flush(&self, deadline: Keep the\n            // runtime safe for callers that construct this type directly.\n            interval: Duration::from_secs(interval_secs.max(1)),\n            last_check: None,\n            check,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Whether automatic upgrade checks are enabled.\n    pub fn enabled(&self) -> bool {\n        self.enabled\n    }\n\n    /// Configured interval between checks.\n    pub fn interval(&self) -> Duration {\n        self.interval\n    }\n\n    /// Poll using the current monotonic time.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `true` when a check was attempted, including when the checker\n    /// reported an error. The error is logged and the supervisor continues;\n    /// the checker is responsible for emitting failure telemetry.\n    pub fn poll(&mut self, telemetry: &Telemetry) -> bool {\n        self.poll_at(telemetry, Instant::now())\n    }\n\n    /// Poll at an explicit monotonic time. This keeps interval behavior\n    /// deterministic in integration tests without sleeping for real hours.\n    pub fn poll_at(&mut self, telemetry: &Telemetry, now: Instant) -> bool {\n        if !self.enabled\n            || self\n                .last_check\n                .is_some_and(|last| now.duration_since(last) < self.interval)\n        {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        self.last_check = Some(now);\n        if let Err(error) = (self.check)(telemetry) {\n            tracing::warn!(error = %error, \"automatic upgrade check failed\");\n        }\n        true\n    }\n}\n\n/// Supervisor configuration.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]\npub struct SupervisorConfig {\n    /// Workspace to monitor.\n    pub workspace: PathBuf,\n    /// Maximum number of concurrent workers.\n    #[serde(default = \"SupervisorConfig::default_max_workers\")]\n    pub max_workers: u32,\n    /// Polling interval for ready queue (seconds).\n    #[serde(default = \"SupervisorConfig::default_poll_interval_secs\")]\n    pub poll_interval_secs: u64,\n    /// Agent adapter to use for spawned workers.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub agent: Option<String>,\n    /// Agent timeout in seconds.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub agent_timeout: Option<u64>,\n    /// Explicit override for the worker binary path (`worker.worker_binary_path`).\n    /// When `None`, the supervisor resolves `std::env::current_exe()`.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub worker_binary_path: Option<PathBuf>,\n    /// Whether the supervisor periodically checks for GitHub releases.\n    #[serde(default = \"SupervisorConfig::default_auto_upgrade_check\")]\n    pub auto_upgrade_check: bool,\n    /// Seconds between automatic GitHub release checks.\n    #[serde(default = \"SupervisorConfig::default_update_check_interval_secs\")]\n    pub update_check_interval_secs: u64,\n}\n\nimpl Default for SupervisorConfig {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        SupervisorConfig {\n            workspace: std::env::current_dir().unwrap_or_else(|_| PathBuf::from(\".\")),\n            max_workers: Self::default_max_workers(),\n            poll_interval_secs: Self::default_poll_interval_secs(),\n            agent: None,\n            agent_timeout: None,\n            worker_binary_path: None,\n            auto_upgrade_check: Self::default_auto_upgrade_check(),\n            update_check_interval_secs: Self::default_update_check_interval_secs(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl SupervisorConfig {\n    pub fn default_max_workers() -> u32 {\n        4\n    }\n\n    pub fn default_poll_interval_secs() -> u64 {\n        DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL_SECS\n    }\n\n    pub fn default_auto_upgrade_check() -> bool {\n        false\n    }\n\n    pub fn default_update_check_interval_secs() -> u64 {\n        DEFAULT_UPDATE_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECS\n    }\n\n    /// Load supervisor configuration from a file (TOML, YAML, or JSON).\n    ///\n    /// Supported formats: `.toml`, `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.json`\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `path` - Path to the configuration file\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// * `Ok(SupervisorConfig)` - Loaded configuration\n    /// * `Err(anyhow::Error)` - If file cannot be read or parsed\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```ignore\n    /// use std::path::PathBuf;\n    ///\n    /// let config = SupervisorConfig::from_file(PathBuf::from(\"supervisor-config.yaml\"))?;\n    /// ```\n    pub fn from_file<P: AsRef<Path>>(path: P) -> Result<Self> {\n        let path = path.as_ref();\n        let text = std::fs::read_to_string(path).with_context(|| {\n            format!(\"failed to read supervisor config file: {}\", path.display())\n        })?;\n\n        // Determine format from file extension\n        let config = match path.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()) {\n            Some(\"toml\") => {\n                let config: SupervisorConfig = toml::from_str(&text)\n                    .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid TOML in supervisor config file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n                config\n            }\n            Some(\"yaml\") | Some(\"yml\") => {\n                let config: SupervisorConfig = serde_yaml::from_str(&text)\n                    .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid YAML in supervisor config file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n                config\n            }\n            Some(\"json\") => {\n                let config: SupervisorConfig = serde_json::from_str(&text)\n                    .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid JSON in supervisor config file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n                config\n            }\n            Some(ext) => bail!(\"unsupported supervisor config file extension: .{} (supported: .toml, .yaml, .yml, .json)\", ext),\n            None => bail!(\"supervisor config file has no extension (supported: .toml, .yaml, .yml, .json)\"),\n        };\n\n        Ok(config)\n    }\n\n    /// Create a supervisor config from a NEEDLE Config structure.\n    ///\n    /// Extracts supervisor-relevant settings from the full NEEDLE config\n    /// and returns a SupervisorConfig ready for use.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `config` - Full NEEDLE configuration\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// * `SupervisorConfig` - Configuration for supervisor\n    pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Self {\n        SupervisorConfig {\n            workspace: config.workspace.default.clone(),\n            max_workers: config.worker.max_workers,\n            poll_interval_secs: DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL_SECS,\n            agent: Some(config.agent.default.clone()),\n            agent_timeout: Some(config.agent.timeout),\n            worker_binary_path: config.worker.worker_binary_path.clone(),\n            auto_upgrade_check: config.supervisor.auto_upgrade_check,\n            update_check_interval_secs: config.supervisor.update_check_interval_secs,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Fleet supervisor state.\npub struct Supervisor {\n    /// Supervisor configuration.\n    config: SupervisorConfig,\n    /// Full NEEDLE configuration.\n    needle_config: Config,\n    /// Bead store for polling the ready queue.\n    store: Arc<dyn BeadStore>,\n    /// Worker registry for tracking active workers.\n    registry: Registry,\n    /// Telemetry instance.\n    telemetry: Telemetry,\n    /// Shutdown flag for graceful termination.\n    shutdown: Arc<AtomicBool>,\n    /// Periodic GitHub release checker.\n    upgrade_poller: UpgradePoller,\n}\n\n/// Source of the resolved worker binary path.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\n#[allow(dead_code)] // Only used in tests\nenum BinarySource {\n    /// Explicit override from `worker.worker_binary_path` config.\n    ConfigOverride,\n    /// Resolved via `std::env::current_exe()`.\n    CurrentExe,\n    /// Fallback to PATH lookup of \"needle\" (when current_exe fails).\n    PathLookup,\n}\n\n/// Result of binary path resolution.\n#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\n#[allow(dead_code)] // Only used in tests\nstruct ResolvedBinary {\n    /// The resolved path to the worker binary.\n    path: PathBuf,\n    /// The source/method used to resolve the path.\n    source: BinarySource,\n}\n\n/// Resolve the worker binary path.\n///\n/// Takes an optional config override path. If provided, uses that path directly.\n/// Otherwise, returns the result of `std::env::current_exe()`.\n/// Handles current_exe() errors gracefully by logging and returning an error.\n///\n/// This fixes GitHub issue jedarden/NEEDLE#11, where a supervisor spawning\n/// workers via bare \"needle\" PATH lookup could accidentally invoke a different\n/// binary occupying that name. Using current_exe() by default ensures the\n/// supervisor always spawns workers from its own binary path (supervisor and\n/// worker are the same binary in the normal case).\n///\n/// **Implementation context:** The pre-#11 behavior was `Command::new(\"needle\")`,\n/// which resolved from $PATH at spawn time. In the reporter's migration, a\n/// legacy tool occupied the name \"needle\" on $PATH, causing supervisors to\n/// believe they were spawning workers (cap=3, 5 ready beads) while worker\n/// heartbeats stayed at 0 for 60 seconds — they were silently invoking the\n/// wrong binary. This fix changes the default resolution to `std::env::current_exe()`\n/// with an optional `worker.worker_binary_path` config override for cases where\n/// the running binary's path is deliberately not what should be spawned (e.g.\n/// a wrapper script).\n///\n/// See ADR-009 (External-Adopter Hardening) for full context.\n/// See GitHub issue: https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/issues/11\n///\n/// # Arguments\n/// * `override_path` - Optional config override for worker binary path\n///\n/// # Returns\n/// * `Ok(PathBuf)` - The resolved worker binary path\n/// * `Err(anyhow::Error)` - If current_exe() fails (and no override provided)\n///\n/// # Examples\n/// ```ignore\n/// use std::path::PathBuf;\n///\n/// // With explicit override\n/// let override_path = Some(PathBuf::from(\"/opt/custom/needle\"));\n/// let path = resolve_worker_binary(override_path)?;\n///\n/// // Without override (uses current_exe)\n/// let path = resolve_worker_binary(None)?;\n/// ```\npub fn resolve_worker_binary(override_path: Option<PathBuf>) -> Result<PathBuf, anyhow::Error> {\n    if let Some(path) = override_path {\n        tracing::debug!(\n            worker_binary = %path.display(),\n            \"using explicit worker binary path from config\"\n        );\n        return Ok(path);\n    }\n\n    std::env::current_exe().context(\"failed to resolve current_exe for worker binary\")\n}\n\n/// Resolve the binary path `needle supervise` spawns workers from.\n///\n/// Prefers an explicit `worker.worker_binary_path` override; otherwise\n/// resolves `std::env::current_exe()`, since the supervisor and worker are\n/// the same binary. Falls back to a bare `\"needle\"` PATH lookup only if\n/// `current_exe()` itself fails (e.g. the executable was deleted after\n/// launch) — this is the previous behavior, now a last resort rather than\n/// the only behavior. See GitHub issue jedarden/NEEDLE#11.\n///\n/// Returns both the resolved path and the source used for resolution.\n#[allow(dead_code)] // Only used in tests\nfn resolve_worker_binary_with_source(override_path: Option<&PathBuf>) -> ResolvedBinary {\n    if let Some(path) = override_path {\n        return ResolvedBinary {\n            path: path.clone(),\n            source: BinarySource::ConfigOverride,\n        };\n    }\n\n    match std::env::current_exe() {\n        Ok(path) => ResolvedBinary {\n            path,\n            source: BinarySource::CurrentExe,\n        },\n        Err(e) => {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                error = %e,\n                \"failed to resolve current_exe for worker spawn, falling back to PATH lookup of 'needle'\"\n            );\n            ResolvedBinary {\n                path: PathBuf::from(\"needle\"),\n                source: BinarySource::PathLookup,\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Supervisor {\n    /// Create a new supervisor with the given configuration.\n    pub fn new(config: SupervisorConfig, needle_config: Config) -> Result<Self> {\n        // Resolve and log worker binary path at startup\n        let worker_binary = resolve_worker_binary(config.worker_binary_path.clone())\n            .context(\"failed to resolve worker binary path for supervisor\")?;\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            worker_binary = %worker_binary.display(),\n            \"Resolved worker binary: {}\",\n            worker_binary.display()\n        );\n\n        // Initialize bead store\n        let store: Arc<dyn BeadStore> = discover_default(\n            config.workspace.clone(),\n            None,\n            Some(\"needle\".to_string()),\n            Some(env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\").to_string()),\n        )\n        .context(\"failed to initialize bead store for supervisor\")?;\n\n        // Initialize registry\n        let registry = Registry::default_location(&needle_config.workspace.home);\n\n        // Initialize telemetry\n        let qualified_id = \"supervisor\".to_string();\n        let telemetry = Telemetry::from_config(qualified_id.clone(), &needle_config.telemetry)\n            .unwrap_or_else(|e| {\n                tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"failed to create telemetry for supervisor, falling back\");\n                Telemetry::new(qualified_id)\n            });\n\n        let upgrade_poller =\n            UpgradePoller::new(config.auto_upgrade_check, config.update_check_interval_secs);\n\n        Ok(Supervisor {\n            config,\n            needle_config,\n            store,\n            registry,\n            telemetry,\n            shutdown: Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false)),\n            upgrade_poller,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Run the supervisor loop until shutdown is signaled.\n    pub async fn run(mut self) -> Result<()> {\n        // Install signal handlers for graceful shutdown\n        let shutdown = self.shutdown.clone();\n        #[cfg(unix)]\n        {\n            // Handle SIGINT and SIGTERM\n            std::mem::drop(tokio::spawn(async move {\n                use tokio::signal::unix::{signal, SignalKind};\n                let mut sigint =\n                    signal(SignalKind::interrupt()).expect(\"failed to setup SIGINT handler\");\n                let mut sigterm =\n                    signal(SignalKind::terminate()).expect(\"failed to setup SIGTERM handler\");\n\n                tokio::select! {\n                    _ = sigint.recv() => {\n                        tracing::info!(\"received SIGINT, shutting down supervisor\");\n                        shutdown.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);\n                    }\n                    _ = sigterm.recv() => {\n                        tracing::info!(\"received SIGTERM, shutting down supervisor\");\n                        shutdown.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);\n                    }\n                }\n            }));\n        }\n\n        #[cfg(not(unix))]\n        {\n            // Handle Ctrl+C on non-Unix platforms\n            let _ = tokio::spawn(async move {\n                if tokio::signal::ctrl_c().await.is_ok() {\n                    tracing::info!(\"received Ctrl+C, shutting down supervisor\");\n                    shutdown.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);\n                }\n            });\n        }\n\n        // Start telemetry\n        self.telemetry.start();\n\n        // Emit worker binary resolved event (fixes GitHub issue jedarden/NEEDLE#11)\n        let worker_binary = resolve_worker_binary(self.config.worker_binary_path.clone())\n            .context(\"failed to resolve worker binary path for supervisor\")?;\n        let binary_source = if self.config.worker_binary_path.is_some() {\n            \"config override (worker.worker_binary_path)\"\n        } else {\n            \"current_exe()\"\n        };\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorBinaryResolved {\n            worker_binary: worker_binary.display().to_string(),\n            source: binary_source.to_string(),\n        })?;\n\n        // Emit supervisor started event\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorStarted {\n            workspace: self.config.workspace.display().to_string(),\n            max_workers: self.config.max_workers,\n        })?;\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            workspace = %self.config.workspace.display(),\n            max_workers = self.config.max_workers,\n            poll_interval_secs = self.config.poll_interval_secs,\n            \"supervisor started\"\n        );\n\n        let mut consecutive_errors = 0u32;\n        let mut last_spawn_time = Instant::now();\n        let mut total_spawned = 0u64;\n        let mut total_polls = 0u64;\n\n        // Main supervisor loop\n        loop {\n            // Check for shutdown signal\n            if self.shutdown.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {\n                tracing::info!(\"shutdown signal received, stopping supervisor\");\n                break;\n            }\n\n            // Enforce spawn backoff\n            let backoff_remaining = last_spawn_time.elapsed().as_secs();\n            if backoff_remaining < SPAWN_BACKOFF_SECS {\n                let wait_secs = SPAWN_BACKOFF_SECS - backoff_remaining;\n                tracing::debug!(wait_secs, \"in spawn backoff, waiting before next poll\");\n                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(wait_secs)).await;\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Poll the ready queue and check fleet state\n            total_polls += 1;\n\n            // Emit summary every 60 ticks (approximately 10 minutes at default interval)\n            if total_polls % 60 == 0 {\n                let active_workers = self.registry.list().unwrap_or_default();\n                let ready_beads = self\n                    .store\n                    .ready(&Filters::default())\n                    .await\n                    .unwrap_or_default();\n                let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorSummary {\n                    polls: total_polls,\n                    spawned: total_spawned,\n                    total_workers: active_workers.len() as u32,\n                    ready_beads: ready_beads.len() as u32,\n                });\n            }\n\n            match self.tick().await {\n                Ok(spawned) => {\n                    consecutive_errors = 0;\n                    if spawned {\n                        total_spawned += 1;\n                        last_spawn_time = Instant::now();\n                    }\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    consecutive_errors += 1;\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        error = %e,\n                        consecutive_errors = consecutive_errors,\n                        \"supervisor tick failed\"\n                    );\n\n                    // Emit spawn failed event\n                    let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorSpawnFailed {\n                        error: e.to_string(),\n                    });\n\n                    // Enter long backoff if error threshold exceeded\n                    if consecutive_errors >= MAX_CONSECUTIVE_ERRORS {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            consecutive_errors,\n                            backoff_secs = ERROR_BACKOFF_SECS,\n                            \"error threshold exceeded, entering long backoff\"\n                        );\n\n                        // Emit backoff event\n                        let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorBackoff {\n                            backoff_secs: ERROR_BACKOFF_SECS,\n                            consecutive_failures: consecutive_errors,\n                        });\n\n                        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(ERROR_BACKOFF_SECS)).await;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Wait before next poll\n            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(self.config.poll_interval_secs)).await;\n        }\n\n        // Emit supervisor stopped event\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorStopped {\n            reason: \"shutdown_requested\".to_string(),\n        })?;\n\n        // Shutdown telemetry\n        self.telemetry.shutdown().await;\n\n        tracing::info!(\"supervisor stopped\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Single supervisor tick: poll queue and spawn workers if needed.\n    ///\n    /// Returns true if a worker was spawned, false otherwise.\n    async fn tick(&mut self) -> Result<bool> {\n        reap_zombie_children();\n\n        // Check independently of queue depth and worker capacity so a full or\n        // idle fleet still notices an available release.\n        self.upgrade_poller.poll(&self.telemetry);\n\n        // Get active workers\n        let active_workers = self.registry.list().unwrap_or_default();\n        let active_count = active_workers.len() as u32;\n\n        // Filter out dead workers (PID no longer alive)\n        let alive_workers: Vec<_> = active_workers\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|w| is_pid_alive(w.pid))\n            .collect();\n\n        // Update registry to remove dead workers\n        if alive_workers.len() < active_workers.len() {\n            tracing::debug!(\n                removed = active_count - alive_workers.len() as u32,\n                \"cleaning up dead workers from registry\"\n            );\n            for worker in &active_workers {\n                if !is_pid_alive(worker.pid) {\n                    let _ = self.registry.deregister(&worker.id);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        let alive_count = alive_workers.len() as u32;\n\n        // Check if we're at capacity\n        if alive_count >= self.config.max_workers {\n            tracing::debug!(\n                alive_count,\n                max_workers = self.config.max_workers,\n                \"fleet at capacity, no spawning needed\"\n            );\n            return Ok(false);\n        }\n\n        // Poll the ready queue\n        let filters = Filters::default();\n        let ready_beads = self.store.ready(&filters).await?;\n\n        // If queue is empty, no need to spawn\n        if ready_beads.is_empty() {\n            tracing::debug!(\"ready queue empty, no spawning needed\");\n            return Ok(false);\n        }\n\n        // We have ready beads and capacity: spawn a worker\n        let ready_count = ready_beads.len();\n        tracing::info!(\n            ready_beads = ready_count,\n            active_workers = alive_count,\n            max_workers = self.config.max_workers,\n            \"ready beads detected with capacity, spawning worker\"\n        );\n\n        // Emit spawn decision event\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorSpawnDecision {\n            to_spawn: 1,\n            ready_beads: ready_count as u32,\n            max_workers: self.config.max_workers,\n        })?;\n\n        // Spawn the worker\n        self.spawn_worker(ready_count).await?;\n\n        Ok(true)\n    }\n\n    /// Spawn a new worker process.\n    async fn spawn_worker(&self, ready_count: usize) -> Result<()> {\n        // Phase 1: resource check before worker spawn.\n        // Check system resources (CPU and memory) before spawning a worker.\n        // If saturated, retry with bounded backoff rather than proceeding into\n        // a launch that may be killed by the OS due to resource pressure.\n        const MAX_RESOURCE_WAIT_SECS: u64 = 120; // Maximum total wait time\n        const RESOURCE_RETRY_DELAY_SECS: u64 = 5; // Initial retry delay\n        let mut resource_wait_total = 0u64;\n        let mut resource_retry_delay = RESOURCE_RETRY_DELAY_SECS;\n\n        loop {\n            match crate::rate_limit::RateLimiter::check_system_resources_for_launch(\n                self.needle_config.worker.cpu_load_warn,\n                self.needle_config.worker.memory_free_warn_mb,\n                &self.telemetry,\n            ) {\n                Ok(()) => {\n                    // Resources are acceptable, proceed to spawn\n                    break;\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    if resource_wait_total >= MAX_RESOURCE_WAIT_SECS {\n                        // Still saturated after max wait, fail the spawn explicitly\n                        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorSpawnFailed {\n                            error: format!(\n                                \"system still saturated after {}s wait: {}\",\n                                MAX_RESOURCE_WAIT_SECS, e\n                            ),\n                        })?;\n                        bail!(\n                            \"worker spawn deferred {} times ({}s total wait), system still saturated: {}. Spawn aborted — retry when load drops\",\n                            resource_wait_total / resource_retry_delay,\n                            resource_wait_total,\n                            e\n                        );\n                    }\n\n                    // Resources are saturated, wait and retry\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        error = %e,\n                        wait_secs = resource_retry_delay,\n                        total_waited_secs = resource_wait_total,\n                        \"system resources saturated, deferring worker spawn\"\n                    );\n\n                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorSpawnFailed {\n                        error: format!(\"system saturated: {}\", e),\n                    })?;\n\n                    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(resource_retry_delay)).await;\n                    resource_wait_total += resource_retry_delay;\n\n                    // Exponential backoff with cap at 30 seconds\n                    resource_retry_delay = std::cmp::min(resource_retry_delay * 2, 30);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        let worker_id = self.generate_worker_id()?;\n        let agent_name = self\n            .config\n            .agent\n            .as_ref()\n            .unwrap_or(&self.needle_config.agent.default)\n            .clone();\n\n        // Resolve the worker binary path. Call resolve_worker_binary() instead\n        // of hardcoding 'needle' to ensure the correct binary is spawned.\n        // Handle resolution errors gracefully by logging and returning an error.\n        let worker_binary = resolve_worker_binary(self.config.worker_binary_path.clone())\n            .with_context(|| {\n                format!(\n                    \"failed to resolve worker binary path for worker {}\",\n                    worker_id\n                )\n            })?;\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            worker_id = %worker_id,\n            agent = %agent_name,\n            worker_binary = %worker_binary.display(),\n            \"spawning worker\"\n        );\n\n        // Spawn the worker process (platform-agnostic) with retry wrapper to\n        // handle ETXTBSY (errno 26) which can occur when spawning a worker binary\n        // that was written to disk immediately before execution (race condition\n        // between write close and kernel page cache sync). This is especially\n        // common after hot-reload or upgrade.\n        //\n        // Uses the resolved worker binary path (current_exe() by default) rather\n        // than a bare PATH lookup of \"needle\" — see GitHub issue jedarden/NEEDLE#11.\n        let _child = crate::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential_child(\n            || {\n                let mut cmd = std::process::Command::new(&worker_binary);\n                cmd.arg(\"run\")\n                    .arg(\"--workspace\")\n                    .arg(&self.config.workspace)\n                    .arg(\"--agent\")\n                    .arg(&agent_name)\n                    .arg(\"--identifier\")\n                    .arg(&worker_id)\n                    .arg(\"--count\")\n                    .arg(\"1\");\n\n                if let Some(timeout) = self.config.agent_timeout {\n                    cmd.arg(\"--timeout\").arg(timeout.to_string());\n                }\n\n                // Spawn in background (detached process)\n                cmd.stdin(std::process::Stdio::null())\n                    .stdout(std::process::Stdio::null())\n                    .stderr(std::process::Stdio::null());\n\n                #[cfg(unix)]\n                {\n                    use std::os::unix::process::CommandExt;\n                    cmd.process_group(0);\n\n                    // On Unix, use setsid to create a new session\n                    unsafe {\n                        cmd.pre_exec(|| {\n                            libc::setsid();\n                            Ok(())\n                        });\n                    }\n                }\n\n                cmd.spawn()\n            },\n            10,\n            20,\n        )?;\n\n        // Emit worker spawned event\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorWorkerSpawned {\n            ready_count,\n            total_spawned: 1,\n        })?;\n\n        tracing::info!(worker_id = %worker_id, \"worker spawned successfully\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Generate a unique worker identifier not currently in use.\n    fn generate_worker_id(&self) -> Result<String> {\n        const NATO_ALPHABET: &[&str] = &[\n            \"alpha\", \"bravo\", \"charlie\", \"delta\", \"echo\", \"foxtrot\", \"golf\", \"hotel\", \"india\",\n            \"juliet\", \"kilo\", \"lima\", \"mike\", \"november\", \"oscar\", \"papa\", \"quebec\", \"romeo\",\n            \"sierra\", \"tango\", \"uniform\", \"victor\", \"whiskey\", \"xray\", \"yankee\", \"zulu\",\n        ];\n\n        let active = self.registry.list().unwrap_or_default();\n        let occupied: std::collections::HashSet<String> = active\n            .iter()\n            .map(|w| w.id.split('-').next_back().unwrap_or(&w.id).to_string())\n            .collect();\n\n        for name in NATO_ALPHABET {\n            if !occupied.contains(*name) {\n                return Ok(name.to_string());\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Fallback: use a numbered suffix\n        for i in 1..=100 {\n            let name = format!(\"worker{}\", i);\n            if !occupied.contains(&name) {\n                return Ok(name);\n            }\n        }\n\n        anyhow::bail!(\"unable to generate unique worker identifier\")\n    }\n}\n\n/// Reap any exited direct children of this process (workers spawned by\n/// `Supervisor::spawn_worker`) so they don't accumulate as `<defunct>`\n/// zombies for the lifetime of the supervisor daemon.\n///\n/// Safe to call unconditionally every tick: `needle supervise` only ever\n/// directly spawns worker processes — gate commands and dispatch\n/// subprocesses are spawned by the *worker* process, a separate PID tree —\n/// so a blind `waitpid(-1, ...)` here cannot race with `.wait()` calls\n/// elsewhere in the codebase (`dispatch`/`telemetry`/`canary`), which all\n/// run in different processes. See ADR-010 / GH #12.\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn reap_zombie_children() {\n    reap_children_matching(-1);\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(unix))]\nfn reap_zombie_children() {}\n\n/// Shared implementation of the `WNOHANG` reap loop, parameterized by which\n/// PID to wait on (`-1` in production, meaning \"any direct child\" — see\n/// `reap_zombie_children`). Split out so tests can exercise the exact same\n/// loop scoped to a single PID they spawned themselves, instead of calling\n/// the crate-wide `-1` sweep from inside the shared `cargo test --lib`\n/// process, where it could reap an unrelated concurrently-running test's own\n/// child (unit tests across the whole crate share one process/many threads,\n/// unlike separate integration-test binaries).\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn reap_children_matching(target_pid: libc::pid_t) {\n    loop {\n        let mut status: libc::c_int = 0;\n        // SAFETY: waitpid(target_pid, &mut status, WNOHANG) reaps an\n        // already-exited child (any direct child, if target_pid == -1)\n        // without blocking; `status` is a valid stack-local out parameter\n        // for the duration of the call.\n        let pid = unsafe { libc::waitpid(target_pid, &mut status, libc::WNOHANG) };\n        match pid {\n            0 => break,          // No exited children ready to reap right now.\n            n if n < 0 => break, // ECHILD (no children) or another errno; stop for this tick.\n            n => tracing::debug!(reaped_pid = n, \"reaped exited worker child\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Run the supervisor from the CLI.\n///\n/// This is the entry point for `needle supervise`.\npub async fn run_supervisor(workspace_opt: Option<PathBuf>) -> Result<()> {\n    // Determine workspace\n    let workspace_root = if let Some(ws) = workspace_opt {\n        ws.canonicalize().unwrap_or_else(|_| ws.clone())\n    } else {\n        let global = ConfigLoader::load_global()?;\n        global.workspace.default.clone()\n    };\n\n    // Load full config\n    let cli_overrides = CliOverrides {\n        workspace: Some(workspace_root.clone()),\n        ..Default::default()\n    };\n    let (config, _) = ConfigLoader::load_resolved(&workspace_root, cli_overrides)?;\n\n    // Build supervisor config\n    let supervisor_config = SupervisorConfig {\n        workspace: workspace_root.clone(),\n        max_workers: config.worker.max_workers,\n        poll_interval_secs: DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL_SECS,\n        agent: Some(config.agent.default.clone()),\n        agent_timeout: Some(config.agent.timeout),\n        worker_binary_path: config.worker.worker_binary_path.clone(),\n        auto_upgrade_check: config.supervisor.auto_upgrade_check,\n        update_check_interval_secs: config.supervisor.update_check_interval_secs,\n    };\n\n    // Create and run supervisor\n    let supervisor = Supervisor::new(supervisor_config, config)?;\n    supervisor.run().await\n}\n\n// ─── Tests ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n issue jedarden/NEEDLE#12) ──\n\n    #[cfg(unix)]\n    #[test]\n    fn reap_zombie_children_reaps_an_exited_child() {\n        // Exercises reap_children_matching (the exact loop reap_zombie_children\n        // wraps) scoped to a PID we spawned ourselves — NOT the real\n        // reap_zombie_children()'s `-1` (any child) target. Unit tests across\n        // the whole crate share one process/many threads under `cargo test\n        // --lib`; calling the `-1` sweep here could reap an unrelated,\n        // concurrently-running test's own child out from under it. Scoping to\n        // our own PID exercises the identical waitpid/WNOHANG logic with none\n        // of that collision risk.\n        //\n        // Spawn a real short-lived child directly (no setsid/detach — this\n        // test process is its real parent).\n        let child = std::process::Command::new(\"true\")\n            .spawn()\n            .expect(\"failed to spawn `true`\");\n        let pid = child.id();\n\n        // Wait for it to actually exit (without reaping it — do not call\n        // child.wait() here, that would reap it ourselves and defeat the test).\n        let stat_path = format!(\"/proc/{pid}/stat\");\n        let mut became_zombie = false;\n        for _ in 0..200 {\n            if let Ok(stat) = std::fs::read_to_string(&stat_path) {\n                if let Some(after_comm) = stat.rfind(')') {\n                    if stat[after_comm + 1..].trim_start().starts_with('Z') {\n                        became_zombie = true;\n                        break;\n                    }\n                }\n            } else {\n                // Already reaped by something else, or /proc entry gone —\n                // can't validate the pre-condition; skip rather than false-fail.\n                break;\n            }\n            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(10));\n        }\n        assert!(\n            became_zombie,\n            \"child did not reach zombie state before timeout — test precondition not met\"\n        );\n\n        reap_children_matching(pid as libc::pid_t);\n\n        // After reaping, /proc/<pid> should no longer exist.\n        assert!(\n            !std::path::Path::new(&stat_path).exists(),\n            \"child was not reaped: {stat_path} still exists\"\n        );\n\n        // Prevent a double-wait/drop warning: the child is already reaped by\n        // our sweep, so explicitly forget rather than calling child.wait().\n        std::mem::forget(child);\n    }\n\n    // ── Supervisor startup resolved path logging test (bf-5hnpy) ──\n\n    #[tokio::test]\n    async fn supervisor_emits_binary_resolved_event_on_startup() {\n        use crate::config::{AgentConfig, Config,
