\"debug\", context, Some(bead_id.clone()))\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Log querying ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Parse a `--since` value into a `DateTime<Utc>`.\n///\n/// Accepts relative durations like `1h`, `30m`, `24h`, `7d` or absolute\n/// ISO 8601 / date strings like `2026-03-20` or `2026-03-20T15:00:00Z`.\npub fn parse_since(input: &str) -> Result<DateTime<Utc>> {\n    let trimmed = input.trim();\n\n    // Try relative duration: Nh, Nm, Nd, Ns\n    if let Some(rest) = trimmed.strip_suffix('h') {\n        let hours: i64 = rest.parse().context(\"invalid hours in --since\")?;\n        return Ok(Utc::now() - chrono::Duration::hours(hours));\n    }\n    if let Some(rest) = trimmed.strip_suffix('m') {\n        let mins: i64 = rest.parse().context(\"invalid minutes in --since\")?;\n        return Ok(Utc::now() - chrono::Duration::minutes(mins));\n    }\n    if let Some(rest) = trimmed.strip_suffix('d') {\n        let days: i64 = rest.parse().context(\"invalid days in --since\")?;\n        return Ok(Utc::now() - chrono::Duration::days(days));\n    }\n    if let Some(rest) = trimmed.strip_suffix('s') {\n        if rest.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) {\n            let secs: i64 = rest.parse().context(\"invalid seconds in --since\")?;\n            return Ok(Utc::now() - chrono::Duration::seconds(secs));\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Try ISO 8601 with time\n    if let Ok(dt) = trimmed.parse::<DateTime<Utc>>() {\n        return Ok(dt);\n    }\n\n    // Try date-only (YYYY-MM-DD) → midnight UTC\n    if let Ok(date) = chrono::NaiveDate::parse_from_str(trimmed, \"%Y-%m-%d\") {\n        let dt = date.and_hms_opt(0, 0, 0).context(\"invalid date\")?;\n        return Ok(DateTime::from_naive_utc_and_offset(dt, Utc));\n    }\n\n    anyhow::bail!(\n        \"unrecognized --since format: '{}'. Use relative (1h, 30m, 7d) or ISO date (2026-03-20)\",\n        input\n    )\n}\n\n/// Convert a glob-style filter pattern to a regex.\n///\n/// Supports `*` as wildcard. E.g., `bead.claim.*` → `^bead\\.claim\\..*$`\npub fn glob_to_regex(pattern: &str) -> Result<regex::Regex> {\n    let mut re = String::from(\"^\");\n    for ch in pattern.chars() {\n        match ch {\n            '*' => re.push_str(\".*\"),\n            '.' => re.push_str(\"\\\\.\"),\n            '?' => re.push('.'),\n            c => re.push(c),\n        }\n    }\n    re.push('$');\n    regex::Regex::new(&re).context(\"invalid filter pattern\")\n}\n\n// ─── Rich filter expressions ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A single filter predicate applied to a telemetry event.\nenum FilterPredicate {\n    /// Glob pattern matched against `event_type` (backward-compatible).\n    EventTypeGlob(regex::Regex),\n    /// Exact case-sensitive match on a named field.\n    FieldEquals { field: String, value: String },\n    /// Regex match on a named field.\n    FieldRegex {\n        field: String,\n        pattern: regex::Regex,\n    },\n    /// Numeric greater-than on a named field.\n    FieldGt { field: String, threshold: f64 },\n}\n\n/// A conjunction (AND) of filter predicates for querying telemetry events.\n///\n/// Build from one or more expression strings with [`LogsFilter::parse`].\npub struct LogsFilter {\n    predicates: Vec<FilterPredicate>,\n}\n\nimpl LogsFilter {\n    /// Parse a list of filter expression strings into a `LogsFilter`.\n    ///\n    /// Each expression may be one of:\n    /// - `field=value`   — exact string match\n    /// - `field~pattern` — regex match\n    /// - `field>number`  — numeric greater-than\n    /// - `glob`          — glob pattern on `event_type` (no operator, backward compat)\n    ///\n    /// All predicates are ANDed together.\n    pub fn parse(exprs: &[&str]) -> Result<Self> {\n        let mut predicates = Vec::with_capacity(exprs.len());\n        for expr in exprs {\n            let expr = expr.trim();\n            if let Some(pos) = expr.find('=') {\n                let field = expr[..pos].to_string();\n                let value = expr[pos + 1..].to_string();\n                predicates.push(FilterPredicate::FieldEquals { field, value });\n            } else if let Some(pos) = expr.find('~') {\n                let field = expr[..pos].to_string();\n                let raw = &expr[pos + 1..];\n                let pattern = regex::Regex::new(raw)\n                    .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid regex in filter '{expr}': {raw}\"))?;\n                predicates.push(FilterPredicate::FieldRegex { field, pattern });\n            } else if let Some(pos) = expr.find('>') {\n                let field = expr[..pos].to_string();\n                let raw = &expr[pos + 1..];\n                let threshold: f64 = raw\n                    .parse()\n                    .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid number in filter '{expr}': {raw}\"))?;\n                predicates.push(FilterPredicate::FieldGt { field, threshold });\n            } else {\n                // Treat as glob pattern on event_type.\n                let re = glob_to_regex(expr)?;\n                predicates.push(FilterPredicate::EventTypeGlob(re));\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(LogsFilter { predicates })\n    }\n\n    /// Return `true` if the event satisfies all predicates.\n    pub fn matches(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> bool {\n        self.predicates.iter().all(|p| predicate_matches(p, event))\n    }\n\n    /// Return `true` if the filter has no predicates (matches everything).\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.predicates.is_empty()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Evaluate a single predicate against an event.\nfn predicate_matches(pred: &FilterPredicate, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> bool {\n    match pred {\n        FilterPredicate::EventTypeGlob(re) => re.is_match(&event.event_type),\n        FilterPredicate::FieldEquals { field, value } => {\n            get_event_field_str(event, field).as_deref() == Some(value.as_str())\n        }\n        FilterPredicate::FieldRegex { field, pattern } => get_event_field_str(event, field)\n            .map(|v| pattern.is_match(&v))\n            .unwrap_or(false),\n        FilterPredicate::FieldGt { field, threshold } => get_event_field_f64(event, field)\n            .map(|v| v > *threshold)\n            .unwrap_or(false),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Extract a named field from a `TelemetryEvent` as a string.\n///\n/// Supported top-level fields: `event_type`, `worker_id`, `session_id`,\n/// `bead_id`, `workspace`. Data sub-fields can be accessed directly by\n/// name (matched against `event.data[field]`).\nfn get_event_field_str(event: &TelemetryEvent, field: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    match field {\n        \"event_type\" => Some(event.event_type.clone()),\n        \"worker_id\" => Some(event.worker_id.clone()),\n        \"session_id\" => Some(event.session_id.clone()),\n        \"bead_id\" => event.bead_id.as_ref().map(|b| b.as_ref().to_string()),\n        \"workspace\" => event.workspace.as_ref().map(|p| p.display().to_string()),\n        _ => {\n            // Check data sub-fields.\n            event.data.get(field).map(|v| match v {\n                serde_json::Value::String(s) => s.clone(),\n                other => other.to_string(),\n            })\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Extract a named field from a `TelemetryEvent` as a float.\n///\n/// Supported numeric fields: `duration_ms`, `sequence`, and any numeric key\n/// in `event.data`.\nfn get_event_field_f64(event: &TelemetryEvent, field: &str) -> Option<f64> {\n    match field {\n        \"duration_ms\" => event.duration_ms.map(|d| d as f64),\n        \"sequence\" => Some(event.sequence as f64),\n        _ => event.data.get(field).and_then(|v| v.as_f64()),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Parse a time-bound string (relative or absolute) into a UTC timestamp.\n///\n/// This is an alias for [`parse_since`] and accepts the same formats.\npub fn parse_until(input: &str) -> Result<DateTime<Utc>> {\n    parse_since(input)\n}\n\n/// Read and parse JSONL log files from a directory.\n///\n/// Returns events sorted by timestamp. Optionally filters by `since`, `until`,\n/// and a [`LogsFilter`] predicate set.\npub fn read_logs(\n    log_dir: &Path,\n    since: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,\n    until: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,\n    filter: Option<&LogsFilter>,\n) -> Result<Vec<TelemetryEvent>> {\n    let mut events = Vec::new();\n\n    if !log_dir.is_dir() {\n        return Ok(events);\n    }\n\n    let entries = std::fs::read_dir(log_dir)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"cannot read log directory: {}\", log_dir.display()))?;\n\n    for entry in entries {\n        let entry = entry?;\n        let path = entry.path();\n        if path.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()) != Some(\"jsonl\") {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let contents = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"cannot read log file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        for line in contents.lines() {\n            if line.trim().is_empty() {\n                continue;\n            }\n            let event: TelemetryEvent = match serde_json::from_str(line) {\n                Ok(e) => e,\n                Err(_) => continue, // Skip malformed lines\n            };\n            if let Some(ref cutoff) = since {\n                if event.timestamp < *cutoff {\n                    continue;\n                }\n            }\n            if let Some(ref ceiling) = until {\n                if event.timestamp > *ceiling {\n                    continue;\n                }\n            }\n            if let Some(f) = filter {\n                if !f.matches(&event) {\n                    continue;\n                }\n            }\n            events.push(event);\n        }\n    }\n\n    events.sort_by_key(|a| a.timestamp);\n    Ok(events)\n}\n\n/// Compute cost summary from effort events.\npub fn compute_cost_summary(events: &[TelemetryEvent]) -> CostSummary {\n    let mut summary = CostSummary::default();\n    for event in events {\n        if event.event_type == \"effort.recorded\" {\n            summary.total_events += 1;\n            if let Some(cost) = event.data[\"estimated_cost_usd\"].as_f64() {\n                summary.total_cost_usd += cost;\n            }\n            if let Some(tokens_in) = event.data[\"tokens_in\"].as_u64() {\n                summary.total_tokens_in += tokens_in;\n            }\n            if let Some(tokens_out) = event.data[\"tokens_out\"].as_u64() {\n                summary.total_tokens_out += tokens_out;\n            }\n            if let Some(elapsed) = event.data[\"elapsed_ms\"].as_u64() {\n                summary.total_elapsed_ms += elapsed;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    summary\n}\n\n/// Aggregated cost data from effort events.\n#[derive(Debug, Default)]\npub struct CostSummary {\n    pub total_events: u64,\n    pub total_cost_usd: f64,\n    pub total_tokens_in: u64,\n    pub total_tokens_out: u64,\n    pub total_elapsed_ms: u64,\n}\n\n/// Per-worker cost breakdown from effort events.\n#[derive(Debug, Default)]\npub struct WorkerCostSummary {\n    pub worker_id: String,\n    pub total_events: u64,\n    pub total_cost_usd: f64,\n    pub total_tokens_in: u64,\n    pub total_tokens_out: u64,\n    pub total_elapsed_ms: u64,\n}\n\n/// Compute per-worker cost breakdown from effort events.\n///\n/// Returns one entry per worker that has at least one effort event, sorted\n/// by descending total cost.\npub fn compute_cost_by_worker(events: &[TelemetryEvent]) -> Vec<WorkerCostSummary> {\n    let mut map: std::collections::HashMap<String, WorkerCostSummary> =\n        std::collections::HashMap::new();\n    for event in events {\n        if event.event_type != \"effort.recorded\" {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let entry = map\n            .entry(event.worker_id.clone())\n            .or_insert_with(|| WorkerCostSummary {\n                worker_id: event.worker_id.clone(),\n                ..Default::default()\n            });\n        entry.total_events += 1;\n        if let Some(cost) = event.data[\"estimated_cost_usd\"].as_f64() {\n            entry.total_cost_usd += cost;\n        }\n        if let Some(tokens_in) = event.data[\"tokens_in\"].as_u64() {\n            entry.total_tokens_in += tokens_in;\n        }\n        if let Some(tokens_out) = event.data[\"tokens_out\"].as_u64() {\n            entry.total_tokens_out += tokens_out;\n        }\n        if let Some(elapsed) = event.data[\"elapsed_ms\"].as_u64() {\n            entry.total_elapsed_ms += elapsed;\n        }\n    }\n    let mut result: Vec<WorkerCostSummary> = map.into_values().collect();\n    result.sort_by(|a, b| {\n        b.total_cost_usd\n            .partial_cmp(&a.total_cost_usd)\n            .unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal)\n    });\n    result\n}\n\n/// Per-workspace cost breakdown from effort events.\n#[derive(Debug, Default)]\npub struct WorkspaceCostSummary {\n    pub workspace: String,\n    pub total_events: u64,\n    pub total_cost_usd: f64,\n    pub total_tokens_in: u64,\n    pub total_tokens_out: u64,\n    pub total_elapsed_ms: u64,\n}\n\n/// Compute per-workspace cost breakdown from effort events.\n///\n/// Returns one entry per workspace that has at least one effort event, sorted\n/// by descending total cost.\npub fn compute_cost_by_workspace(events: &[TelemetryEvent]) -> Vec<WorkspaceCostSummary> {\n    let mut map: std::collections::HashMap<String, WorkspaceCostSummary> =\n        std::collections::HashMap::new();\n    for event in events {\n        if event.event_type != \"effort.recorded\" {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let ws_key = event\n            .workspace\n            .as_ref()\n            .map(|p| p.display().to_string())\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| \"unknown\".to_string());\n        let entry = map\n            .entry(ws_key.clone())\n            .or_insert_with(|| WorkspaceCostSummary {\n                workspace: ws_key,\n                ..Default::default()\n            });\n        entry.total_events += 1;\n        if let Some(cost) = event.data[\"estimated_cost_usd\"].as_f64() {\n            entry.total_cost_usd += cost;\n        }\n        if let Some(tokens_in) = event.data[\"tokens_in\"].as_u64() {\n            entry.total_tokens_in += tokens_in;\n        }\n        if let Some(tokens_out) = event.data[\"tokens_out\"].as_u64() {\n            entry.total_tokens_out += tokens_out;\n        }\n        if let Some(elapsed) = event.data[\"elapsed_ms\"].as_u64() {\n            entry.total_elapsed_ms += elapsed;\n        }\n    }\n    let mut result: Vec<WorkspaceCostSummary> = map.into_values().collect();\n    result.sort_by(|a, b| {\n        b.total_cost_usd\n            .partial_cmp(&a.total_cost_usd)\n            .unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal)\n    });\n    result\n}\n\n// ─── Structured logging macros ─────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Emit a structured log event with the specified level.\n///\n/// This macro provides a convenient way to log structured events with the\n/// telemetry system. It automatically serializes the context to JSON and\n/// emits it through the provided telemetry instance.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `$telemetry` - The telemetry instance to emit through\n/// * `$level` - Log level: \"info\", \"warn\", \"error\", or \"debug\"\n/// * `$phase` - Phase identifier (e.g., \"dispatch\", \"claim\")\n/// * `$context` - JSON object with context data\n/// * `$bead_id` - Optional bead ID\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// # use needle::telemetry::Telemetry;\n/// # use needle::log;\n/// # use needle::types::BeadId;\n/// # let telemetry: Telemetry = unimplemented!();\n/// // Basic info log\n/// log!(telemetry, \"info\", \"dispatch\", {\"status\": \"started\"});\n///\n/// // Log with bead context\n/// let bead_id = BeadId::from(\"needle-123\");\n/// log!(telemetry, \"info\", \"claim\", {\"attempt\": 1}, Some(bead_id));\n///\n/// // Error log with context\n/// log!(telemetry, \"error\", \"outcome\", {\n///     \"exit_code\": 1,\n///     \"reason\": \"timeout\"\n/// }, None::<BeadId>);\n/// ```\n#[macro_export]\nmacro_rules! log {\n    ($telemetry:expr, $level:expr, $phase:expr, {$($key:ident: $value:expr),* $(,)?}) => {\n        $telemetry.log(\n            $phase,\n            $level,\n            $crate::serde_json::json!({ $($key: $value),* }),\n            None,\n        )\n    };\n    ($telemetry:expr, $level:expr, $phase:expr, {$($key:ident: $value:expr),* $(,)?}, $bead_id:expr) => {\n        $telemetry.log(\n            $phase,\n            $level,\n            $crate::serde_json::json!({ $($key: $value),* }),\n            $bead_id,\n        )\n    };\n}\n\n/// Emit an info-level structured log event.\n///\n/// Convenience macro for logging at \"info\" level.\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// # use needle::telemetry::Telemetry;\n/// # use needle::log_info;\n/// # let telemetry: Telemetry = unimplemented!();\n/// log_info!(telemetry, \"dispatch\", {\"status\": \"started\", \"agent\": \"claude\"});\n/// ```\n#[macro_export]\nmacro_rules! log_info {\n    ($telemetry:expr, $phase:expr, {$($key:ident: $value:expr),* $(,)?}) => {\n        $telemetry.log_info($phase, $crate::serde_json::json!({ $($key: $value),* }))\n    };\n    ($telemetry:expr, $phase:expr, {$($key:ident: $value:expr),* $(,)?}, $bead_id:expr) => {\n        $telemetry.log_info_with_bead($phase, $crate::serde_json::json!({ $($key: $value),* }), &$bead_id)\n    };\n}\n\n/// Emit a warn-level structured log event.\n///\n/// Convenience macro for logging at \"warn\" level.\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// # use needle::telemetry::Telemetry;\n/// # use needle::log_warn;\n/// # let telemetry: Telemetry = unimplemented!();\n/// log_warn!(telemetry, \"claim\", {\"reason\": \"race_lost\", \"attempts\": 3});\n/// ```\n#[macro_export]\nmacro_rules! log_warn {\n    ($telemetry:expr, $phase:expr, {$($key:ident: $value:expr),* $(,)?}) => {\n        $telemetry.log_warn($phase, $crate::serde_json::json!({ $($key: $value),* }))\n    };\n    ($telemetry:expr, $phase:expr, {$($key:ident: $value:expr),* $(,)?}, $bead_id:expr) => {\n        $telemetry.log_warn_with_bead($phase, $crate::serde_json::json!({ $($key: $value),* }), &$bead_id)\n    };\n}\n\n/// Emit an error-level structured log event.\n///\n/// Convenience macro for logging at \"error\" level.\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// # use needle::telemetry::Telemetry;\n/// # use needle::log_error;\n/// # let telemetry: Telemetry = unimplemented!();\n/// log_error!(telemetry, \"outcome\", {\"exit_code\": 1, \"error\": \"timeout\"});\n/// ```\n#[macro_export]\nmacro_rules! log_error {\n    ($telemetry:expr, $phase:expr, {$($key:ident: $value:expr),* $(,)?}) => {\n        $telemetry.log_error($phase, $crate::serde_json::json!({ $($key: $value),* }))\n    };\n    ($telemetry:expr, $phase:expr, {$($key:ident: $value:expr),* $(,)?}, $bead_id:expr) => {\n        $telemetry.log_error_with_bead($phase, $crate::serde_json::json!({ $($key: $value),* }), &$bead_id)\n    };\n}\n\n/// Emit a debug-level structured log event.\n///\n/// Convenience macro for logging at \"debug\" level.\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// # use needle::telemetry::Telemetry;\n/// # use needle::log_debug;\n/// # let telemetry: Telemetry = unimplemented!();\n/// log_debug!(telemetry, \"routing\", {\"model\": \"sonnet-4\", \"confidence\": 0.95});\n/// ```\n#[macro_export]\nmacro_rules! log_debug {\n    ($telemetry:expr, $phase:expr, {$($key:ident: $bead_id:expr) => {\n        $telemetry.log_debug_with_bead($phase, $crate::serde_json::json!({ $($key: $value),* }), &$bead_id)\n    };\n}\n\n// ─── Unit tests When a worker hits EXHAUSTED quickly the total telemetry is only a few\n    /// hundred bytes — well below BufWriter's 8 KB auto-flush threshold.\n    /// `shutdown()` must drop the sender (closing the channel) and *await* the\n    /// writer task's JoinHandle so the flush runs before the tokio Runtime drops.\n    #[tokio::test]\n    async fn shutdown_flushes_bufwriter_on_short_lived_session() {\n        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(\"needle-test-shutdown-flush\");\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);\n\n        let (telemetry, path) = Telemetry::with_log_dir_and_path(\"test-worker\".to_string(), &dir)\n            .expect(\"should create\");\n\n        // start() must be called from inside the runtime.\n        telemetry.start();\n\n        // Emit a handful of small events — total << 8 KB BufWriter threshold.\n        telemetry\n            .emit(EventKind::WorkerStarted {\n                worker_name: \"test-worker\".to_string(),\n                version: \"0.1.0\".to_string(),\n            })\n            .unwrap();\n        telemetry.emit(EventKind::QueueEmpty).unwrap();\n        telemetry\n            .emit(EventKind::WorkerStopped {\n                reason: \"exhausted\".to_string(),\n                beads_processed: 0,\n                uptime_secs: 0,\n            })\n            .unwrap();\n\n        // shutdown() closes the channel, awaits the writer task, and guarantees\n        // the BufWriter is flushed before returning — no sleep required.\n        telemetry.shutdown().await;\n\n        // The file must contain the 4 events (worker.booting is written during init,\n        // plus the 3 events emitted by the test). (worker.booting + 3 emitted events)\"\n        );\n        for line in &lines {\n            let v: serde_json::Value =\n                serde_json::from_str(line).expect(\"each line must be valid JSON\");\n            assert!(\n                v.get(\"event_type\").is_some(),\n                \"event_type field must be present\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);\n    }\n\n    /// Verify that events emitted inside an OTel span carry the correct\n    /// trace_id and span_id in 32/16 lowercase-hex W3C format.\n    #[cfg(feature = called on every registered sink during graceful\n    /// shutdown, and the deadline value is forwarded to the sink.\n    #[tokio::test]\n    async fn shutdown_flush_calls_flush_with_deadline() {\n        let deadline_received = Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None::<std::time::Duration>));\n\n        struct DeadlineSink {\n            received: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<std::time::Duration>>>,\n        }\n        impl Sink for DeadlineSink {\n            fn accept(&self, _: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            fn flush(&self, deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {\n                *self.received.lock().unwrap() = Some(deadline);\n                Ok(())\n            }\n        }\n\n        let telemetry = Telemetry::with_boxed_sinks(\n            \"test-deadline\".to_string(),\n            vec![Box::new(DeadlineSink {\n                received: deadline_received.clone(),\n            })],\n        );\n        telemetry.start();\n        telemetry.emit(EventKind::QueueEmpty).unwrap();\n        telemetry.shutdown().await;\n\n        let dl = deadline_received.lock().unwrap();\n        assert!(\n            dl.is_some(),\n            \"flush must be called with a non-None deadline on shutdown\"\n        );\n        assert!(\n            dl.unwrap() > std::time::Duration::ZERO,\n            \"deadline passed to flush must be positive\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// A blocking fake sink whose `flush` sleeps longer than its deadline must\n    /// return an error rather than hanging indefinitely. The bus must not block\n    /// past the deadline.\n    #[tokio::test]\n    async fn shutdown_does_not_hang_when_flush_exceeds_deadline() {\n        struct SlowFlusher;\n        impl Sink for threshold exceeded, entering long backoff\"\n                        );\n\n                        // Emit backoff event\n                        let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorBackoff {\n                            backoff_secs: ERROR_BACKOFF_SECS,\n                            consecutive_failures: consecutive_errors,\n                        });\n\n                        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(ERROR_BACKOFF_SECS)).await;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Wait before next poll\n            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(self.config.poll_interval_secs)).await;\n        }\n\n        // Emit supervisor stopped event\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorStopped {\n            reason: \"shutdown_requested\".to_string(),\n        })?;\n\n        // Shutdown telemetry\n        self.telemetry.shutdown().await;\n\n        tracing::info!(\"supervisor stopped\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Single supervisor tick: poll queue and spawn workers if needed.\n    ///\n    /// Returns true if a worker was spawned, false otherwise.\n    async fn tick(&mut self) -> Result<bool> {\n        reap_zombie_children();\n\n        // Check independently of queue depth and worker capacity so a full or\n        // idle fleet still notices an available release.\n        self.upgrade_poller.poll(&self.telemetry);\n\n        // Check for binary freshness and rotate workers if needed\n        if let Some(checker) = &mut self.binary_freshness {\n            if let Ok(Some(check_result)) = checker.poll() {\n                match check_result {\n                    FreshnessCheck::NewBinary {\n                        binary_path,\n                        old_hash,\n                        new_hash,\n                    } => {\n                        tracing::info!(\n                            old_binary = %self.current_worker_binary.display(),\n                            new_binary = %binary_path.display(),\n                            old_hash = %old_hash[..8],\n                            new_hash = %new_hash[..8],\n                            \"new binary detected, initiating worker rotation\"\n                        );\n\n                        // Emit binary rotation detected event\n                        let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorBinaryRotationDetected {\n                            old_binary: self.current_worker_binary.display().to_string(),\n                            new_binary: binary_path.display().to_string(),\n                            old_hash,\n                            new_hash,\n                        });\n\n                        // Drain existing workers and relaunch with new binary\n                        let _ = self.rotate_workers(&binary_path).await;\n\n                        // Update current worker binary path\n                        self.current_worker_binary = binary_path;\n                    }\n                    FreshnessCheck::BinaryMissing { binary_path } => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            binary = %binary_path.display(),\n                            \"monitored binary missing, skipping rotation check\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                    FreshnessCheck::CheckFailed { error, .. } => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            error = %error,\n                            \"binary freshness check failed\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                    FreshnessCheck::Unchanged { .. } => {\n                        // No change, continue normal operation\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Get active workers\n        let active_workers = self.registry.list().unwrap_or_default();\n        let active_count = active_workers.len() as u32;\n\n        // Filter out dead workers (PID no longer alive)\n        let alive_workers: Vec<_> = active_workers\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|w| is_pid_alive(w.pid))\n            .collect();\n\n        // Update registry to remove dead workers\n        if alive_workers.len() < active_workers.len() {\n            tracing::debug!(\n                removed = active_count - alive_workers.len() as u32,\n                \"cleaning up dead workers from registry\"\n            );\n            for worker in &active_workers {\n                if !is_pid_alive(worker.pid) {\n                    let _ = self.registry.deregister(&worker.id);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        let alive_count = alive_workers.len() as u32;\n\n        // Check if we're at capacity\n        if alive_count >= self.config.max_workers {\n            tracing::debug!(\n                alive_count,\n                max_workers = self.config.max_workers,\n                \"fleet at capacity, no spawning needed\"\n            );\n            return Ok(false);\n        }\n\n        // Poll the ready queue\n        let filters = Filters::default();\n        let ready_beads = self.store.ready(&filters).await?;\n\n        // If queue is empty, no need to spawn\n        if ready_beads.is_empty() {\n            tracing::debug!(\"ready queue empty, no spawning needed\");\n            return Ok(false);\n        }\n\n        // We have ready beads and capacity: spawn a worker\n        let ready_count = ready_beads.len();\n        tracing::info!(\n            ready_beads = ready_count,\n            active_workers = alive_count,\n            max_workers = self.config.max_workers,\n            \"ready beads detected with capacity, spawning worker\"\n        );\n\n        // Emit spawn decision event\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorSpawnDecision {\n            to_spawn: 1,\n            ready_beads: ready_count as u32,\n            max_workers: self.config.max_workers,\n        })?;\n\n        // Spawn the worker\n        self.spawn_worker(ready_count).await?;\n\n        Ok(true)\n    }\n\n    /// Spawn a new worker process.\n    async fn spawn_worker(&self, ready_count: usize) -> Result<()> {\n        // Phase 1: resource check before worker spawn.\n        // Check system resources (CPU and memory) before spawning a worker.\n        // If saturated, retry with bounded backoff rather than proceeding into\n        // a launch that may be killed by the OS due to resource pressure.\n        const MAX_RESOURCE_WAIT_SECS: u64 = 120; // Maximum total wait time\n        const RESOURCE_RETRY_DELAY_SECS: u64 = 5; // Initial retry delay\n        let mut resource_wait_total = 0u64;\n        let mut resource_retry_delay = RESOURCE_RETRY_DELAY_SECS;\n\n        loop {\n            match crate::rate_limit::RateLimiter::check_system_resources_for_launch(\n                self.needle_config.worker.cpu_load_warn,\n                self.needle_config.worker.memory_free_warn_mb,\n                &self.telemetry,\n            ) {\n                Ok(()) => {\n                    // Resources are acceptable, proceed to spawn\n                    break;\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    if resource_wait_total >= MAX_RESOURCE_WAIT_SECS {\n                        // Still saturated after max wait, fail the spawn explicitly\n                        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorSpawnFailed {\n                            error: format!(\n                                \"system still saturated after {}s wait: {}\",\n                                MAX_RESOURCE_WAIT_SECS, e\n                            ),\n                        })?;\n                        bail!(\n                            \"worker spawn deferred {} times ({}s total wait), system still saturated: {}. Spawn aborted — retry when load drops\",\n                            resource_wait_total / resource_retry_delay,\n                            resource_wait_total,\n                            e\n                        );\n                    }\n\n                    // Resources are saturated, wait and retry\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        error = %e,\n                        wait_secs = resource_retry_delay,\n                        total_waited_secs = resource_wait_total,\n                        \"system resources saturated, deferring worker spawn\"\n                    );\n\n                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorSpawnFailed {\n                        error: format!(\"system saturated: {}\", e),\n                    })?;\n\n                    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(resource_retry_delay)).await;\n                    resource_wait_total += resource_retry_delay;\n\n                    // Exponential backoff with cap at 30 seconds\n                    resource_retry_delay = std::cmp::min(resource_retry_delay * 2, 30);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        let worker_id = self.generate_worker_id()?;\n        let agent_name = self\n            .config\n            .agent\n            .as_ref()\n            .unwrap_or(&self.needle_config.agent.default)\n            .clone();\n\n        // Resolve the worker binary path. Call resolve_worker_binary() instead\n        // of hardcoding 'needle' to ensure the correct binary is spawned.\n        // Handle resolution errors gracefully by logging and returning an error.\n        let worker_binary = resolve_worker_binary(self.config.worker_binary_path.clone())\n            .with_context(|| {\n                format!(\n                    \"failed to resolve worker binary path for worker {}\",\n                    worker_id\n                )\n            })?;\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            worker_id = %worker_id,\n            agent = %agent_name,\n            worker_binary = %worker_binary.display(),\n            \"spawning worker\"\n        );\n\n        // Spawn the worker process (platform-agnostic) with retry wrapper to\n        // handle ETXTBSY (errno 26) which can occur when spawning a worker binary\n        // that was written to disk immediately before execution (race condition\n        // between write close and kernel page cache sync). This is especially\n        // common after hot-reload or upgrade.\n        //\n        // Uses the resolved worker binary path (current_exe() by default) rather\n        // than a bare PATH lookup of \"needle\" — see GitHub issue jedarden/NEEDLE#11.\n        let _child = crate::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential_child(\n            || {\n                let mut cmd = std::process::Command::new(&worker_binary);\n                cmd.arg(\"run\")\n                    .arg(\"--workspace\")\n                    .arg(&self.config.workspace)\n                    .arg(\"--agent\")\n                    .arg(&agent_name)\n                    .arg(\"--identifier\")\n                    .arg(&worker_id)\n                    .arg(\"--count\")\n                    .arg(\"1\");\n\n                if let Some(timeout) = self.config.agent_timeout {\n                    cmd.arg(\"--timeout\").arg(timeout.to_string());\n                }\n\n                // Spawn in background (detached process)\n                cmd.stdin(std::process::Stdio::null())\n                    .stdout(std::process::Stdio::null())\n                    .stderr(std::process::Stdio::null());\n\n                #[cfg(unix)]\n                {\n                    use std::os::unix::process::CommandExt;\n                    cmd.process_group(0);\n\n                    // On Unix, use setsid to create a new session\n                    unsafe {\n                        cmd.pre_exec(|| {\n                            libc::setsid();\n                            Ok(())\n                        });\n                    }\n                }\n\n                cmd.spawn()\n            },\n            10,\n            20,\n        )?;\n\n        // Emit worker spawned event\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorWorkerSpawned {\n            ready_count,\n            total_spawned: 1,\n        })?;\n\n        tracing::info!(worker_id = %worker_id, \"worker spawned successfully\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Rotate workers onto a new binary by draining existing workers and relaunching.\n    ///\n    /// This method gracefully shuts down all active workers and then launches new\n    /// workers with the updated binary path. The drain process sends SIGTERM to each\n    /// worker and waits for them to exit cleanly before proceeding.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `new_binary_path` - Path to the new worker binary\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// * `Ok(())` - Rotation completed successfully\n    /// * `Err(anyhow::Error)` - Rotation failed\n    async fn rotate_workers(&self, new_binary_path: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n        const DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECS: u64 = 300; // 5 minutes\n\n        // Prevent concurrent rotation attempts\n        if self\n            .draining_workers\n            .compare_exchange(false, true, Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::Relaxed)\n            .is_err()\n        {\n            tracing::warn!(\"worker rotation already in progress, skipping\");\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n\n        let drain_start = Instant::now();\n\n        // Get current workers\n        let active_workers = self.registry.list().unwrap_or_default();\n        let workers_count = active_workers.len() as u32;\n\n        if workers_count == 0 {\n            tracing::info!(\"no active workers to drain, rotation complete\");\n            self.draining_workers.store(false, Ordering::SeqCst);\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            workers_count,\n            timeout_secs = DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n            \"starting worker drain for binary rotation\"\n        );\n\n        // Emit drain started event\n        let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SupervisorWorkerDrainStarted {\n            active_workers: workers_count,\n            drain_timeout_secs: DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n        });\n\n        // Send SIGTERM to all workers for graceful shutdown\n        #[cfg(unix)]\n        {\n            use libc::{kill, getpid, SIGTERM};\n            for worker in &active_workers {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    worker_id = %worker.id,\n                    pid = worker.pid,\n                    \"sending SIGTERM to worker\"\n                );\n\n                // Send SIGTERM to the worker process group\n                unsafe {\n                    // SIGTERM 15 allows graceful shutdown\n                    if kill(worker.pid as i32, SIGTERM) != 0 {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            worker_id = %worker.id,\n                            pid = worker.pid,\n                            \"failed to send SIGTERM to worker\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        #[cfg(not(unix))]\n        {\n            tracing::warn!(\"worker drain not supported on this platform\");\n            self.draining_workers.store(false, Ordering::SeqCst);\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n\n        // Wait for workers to exit\n        let mut elapsed = 0;\n        while elapsed < DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECS {\n            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(5)).await;\n            elapsed += 5;\n\n            let remaining = self\n                .registry\n                .list()\n                .unwrap_or_default()\n                .into_iter()\n                .filter(|w| is_pid_alive(w.pid))\n                .count();\n\n            if remaining == 0 {\n                tracing::info!(\"all workers drained successfully\");\n                break;\n            }\n\n            tracing::debug!(\n                remaining,\n                elapsed_secs = elapsed,\n                \"waiting for workers to drain\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        // Clean up any remaining workers from registry\n        for worker in &active_workers {\n            let _ = self.registry.deregister(&worker.id);\n        }\n\n        let drain_duration = drain_start.elapsed().as_secs();\n\n        // Emit drain completed event\n        let _ = self\n            .telemetry\n            .emit(EventKind::SupervisorWorkerDrainCompleted {\n                workers_drained: workers_count,\n                duration_secs: drain_duration,\n            });\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            workers_drained = workers_count,\n            duration_secs = drain_duration,\n            \"worker drain completed, relaunching with new binary\"\n        );\n\n        // Relaunch workers with the new binary\n        // We'll spawn the same number of workers that were just drained\n        let agent_name = self\n            .config\n            .agent\n            .as_ref()\n            .unwrap_or(&self.needle_config.agent.default)\n            .clone();\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            workers_count,\n            new_binary = %new_binary_path.display(),\n            \"launching workers with new binary\"\n        );\n\n        for i in 0..workers_count {\n            let worker_id = self.generate_worker_id()?;\n            let ready_count = 0; // No ready count needed for rotation spawns\n\n            tracing::info!(\n                worker_id = %worker_id,\n                binary = %new_binary_path.display(),\n                \"spawning worker with new binary ({}/{})\",\n                i + 1,\n                workers_count\n            );\n\n            // Spawn worker with the new binary path\n            let _child = crate::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential_child(\n                || {\n                    let mut cmd = std::process::Command::new(new_binary_path);\n                    cmd.arg(\"run\")\n                        .arg(\"--workspace\")\n                        .arg(&self.config.workspace)\n                        .arg(\"--agent\")\n                        .arg(&agent_name)\n                        .arg(\"--identifier\")\n                        .arg(&worker_id)\n                        .arg(\"--count\")\n                        .arg(\"1\");\n\n                    if let Some(timeout) = self.config.agent_timeout {\n                        cmd.arg(\"--timeout\").arg(timeout.to_string());\n                    }\n\n                    cmd.stdin(std::process::Stdio::null())\n                        .stdout(std::process::Stdio::null())\n                        .stderr(std::process::Stdio::null());\n\n                    #[cfg(unix)]\n                    {\n                        use std::os::unix::process::CommandExt;\n                        cmd.process_group(0);\n\n                        unsafe {\n                            cmd.pre_exec(|| {\n                                libc::setsid();\n                                Ok(())\n                            });\n                        }\n                    }\n\n                    cmd.spawn()\n                },\n                10,\n                20,\n            )?;\n\n            tracing::debug!(worker_id = %worker_id, \"worker launched successfully\");\n        }\n\n        // Emit worker relaunched event\n        let _ = self\n            .telemetry\n            .emit(EventKind::SupervisorWorkerRelaunched {\n                workers_count,\n                new_binary: new_binary_path.display().to_string(),\n            });\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            workers_count,\n            \"worker rotation completed successfully\"\n        );\n\n        // Clear the draining flag\n        self.draining_workers.store(false, Ordering::SeqCst);\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Generate a unique worker identifier not currently in use.\n    fn generate_worker_id(&self) -> Result<String> {\n        const NATO_ALPHABET: &[&str] = &[\n            \"alpha\", \"bravo\", \"charlie\", \"delta\", \"echo\", \"foxtrot\", \"golf\", \"hotel\", \"india\",\n            \"juliet\", \"kilo\", \"lima\", \"mike\", \"november\", \"oscar\", \"papa\", \"quebec\", \"romeo\",\n            \"sierra\", \"tango\", \"uniform\", \"victor\", \"whiskey\", \"xray\", \"yankee\", \"zulu\",\n        ];\n\n        let active = self.registry.list().unwrap_or_default();\n        let occupied: std::collections::HashSet<String> = active\n            .iter()\n            .map(|w| w.id.split('-').next_back().unwrap_or(&w.id).to_string())\n            .collect();\n\n        for name in NATO_ALPHABET {\n            if !occupied.contains(*name) {\n                return Ok(name.to_string());\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Fallback: use a numbered suffix\n        for i in 1..=100 {\n            let name = format!(\"worker{}\", i);\n            if !occupied.contains(&name) {\n                return Ok(name);\n            }\n        }\n\n        anyhow::bail!(\"unable to generate unique worker identifier\")\n    }\n}\n\n/// Reap any exited direct children of this process (workers spawned by\n/// `Supervisor::spawn_worker`) so they don't accumulate as `<defunct>`\n/// zombies for the lifetime of the supervisor daemon.\n///\n/// Safe to call unconditionally every tick: `needle supervise` only ever\n/// directly spawns worker processes — gate commands and dispatch\n/// subprocesses are spawned by the *worker* process, a separate PID tree —\n/// so a blind `waitpid(-1, ...)` here cannot race with `.wait()` calls\n/// elsewhere in the codebase (`dispatch`/`telemetry`/`canary`), which all\n/// run in different processes. See ADR-010 / GH #12.\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn reap_zombie_children() {\n    reap_children_matching(-1);\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(unix))]\nfn reap_zombie_children() {}\n\n/// Shared implementation of the `WNOHANG` reap loop, parameterized by which\n/// PID to wait on (`-1` in production, meaning \"any direct child\" — see\n/// `reap_zombie_children`). Split out so tests can exercise the exact same\n/// loop scoped to a single PID they spawned themselves, instead of calling\n/// the crate-wide `-1` sweep from inside the shared `cargo test --lib`\n/// process, where it could reap an unrelated concurrently-running test's own\n/// child (unit tests across the whole crate share one process/many threads,\n/// unlike separate integration-test binaries).\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn reap_children_matching(target_pid: libc::pid_t) {\n    loop {\n        let mut status: libc::c_int = 0;\n        // SAFETY: waitpid(target_pid, &mut status, WNOHANG) reaps an\n        // already-exited child (any direct child, if target_pid == -1)\n        // without blocking; `status` is a valid stack-local out parameter\n        // for the duration of the call.\n        let pid = unsafe { libc::waitpid(target_pid, &mut status, libc::WNOHANG) };\n        match pid {\n            0 => break,          // No exited children ready to reap right now.\n            n if n < 0 => break, // ECHILD (no children) or another errno; stop for this tick.\n            n => tracing::debug!(reaped_pid = n, \"reaped exited worker child\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Run the supervisor from the CLI.\n///\n/// This is the entry point for `needle supervise`.\npub async fn run_supervisor(workspace_opt: Option<PathBuf>) -> Result<()> {\n    // Determine workspace\n    let workspace_root = if let Some(ws) = workspace_opt {\n        ws.canonicalize().unwrap_or_else(|_| ws.clone())\n    } else {\n        let global = ConfigLoader::load_global()?;\n        global.workspace.default.clone()\n    };\n\n    // Load full config\n    let cli_overrides = CliOverrides {\n        workspace: Some(workspace_root.clone()),\n        ..Default::default()\n    };\n    let (config, _) = ConfigLoader::load_resolved(&workspace_root, cli_overrides)?;\n\n    // Build supervisor config\n    let supervisor_config = SupervisorConfig {\n        workspace: workspace_root.clone(),\n        max_workers: config.worker.max_workers,\n        poll_interval_secs: DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL_SECS,\n        agent: Some(config.agent.default.clone()),\n        agent_timeout: Some(config.agent.timeout),\n        worker_binary_path: config.worker.worker_binary_path.clone(),\n        auto_upgrade_check: config.supervisor.auto_upgrade_check,\n        update_check_interval_secs: config.supervisor.update_check_interval_secs,\n    };\n\n    // Create and run supervisor\n    let supervisor = Supervisor::new(supervisor_config, config)?;\n    supervisor.run().await\n}\n\n// ─── Tests ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n issue jedarden/NEEDLE#12) ──\n\n    #[cfg(unix)]\n    #[test]\n    fn reap_zombie_children_reaps_an_exited_child() {\n        // Exercises reap_children_matching (the exact loop reap_zombie_children\n        // wraps) scoped to a PID we spawned ourselves — NOT the real\n        // reap_zombie_children()'s `-1` (any child) target. Unit tests across\n        // the whole crate share one process/many threads under `cargo test\n        // --lib`; calling the `-1` sweep here could reap an unrelated,\n        // concurrently-running test's own child out from under it. Scoping to\n        // our own PID exercises the identical waitpid/WNOHANG logic with none\n        // of that collision risk.\n        //\n        // Spawn a real short-lived child directly (no setsid/detach — this\n        // test process is its real parent).\n        let child = std::process::Command::new(\"true\")\n            .spawn()\n            .expect(\"failed to spawn `true`\");\n        let pid = child.id();\n\n        // Wait for it to actually exit (without reaping it — do not call\n        // child.wait() here, that would reap it ourselves and defeat the test).\n        let stat_path = format!(\"/proc/{pid}/stat\");\n        let mut became_zombie = false;\n        for _ in 0..200 {\n            if let Ok(stat) = std::fs::read_to_string(&stat_path) {\n                if let Some(after_comm) = stat.rfind(')') {\n                    if stat[after_comm + 1..].trim_start().starts_with('Z') {\n                        became_zombie = true;\n                        break;\n                    }\n                }\n            } else {\n                // Already reaped by something else, or /proc entry gone —\n                // can't validate the pre-condition; skip rather than false-fail.\n                break;\n            }\n            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(10));\n        }\n        assert!(\n            became_zombie,\n            \"child did not reach zombie state before timeout — test precondition not met\"\n        );\n\n        reap_children_matching(pid as libc::pid_t);\n\n        // After reaping, /proc/<pid> should no longer exist.\n        assert!(\n            !std::path::Path::new(&stat_path).exists(),\n            \"child was not reaped: {stat_path} still exists\"\n        );\n\n        // Prevent a double-wait/drop warning: the child is already reaped by\n        // our sweep, so explicitly forget rather than calling child.wait().\n        std::mem::forget(child);\n    }\n\n    // ── Supervisor crate::canary::CanaryRunner;\nuse crate::claim::Claimer;\nuse crate::commit_hook;\nuse crate::config::{Config, ConfigLoader};\nuse crate::cost::{self, BudgetCheck, EffortData};\nuse crate::telemetry::{EventKind, Telemetry};\nuse crate::types::{AgentOutcome, Bead, BeadId, ClaimResult, IdleAction, Outcome, WorkerState};\nuse crate::upgrade::{self, HotReloadCheck};\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Global shutdown flag for signal handlers\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Global pointer to the shutdown flag, used by synchronous signal handlers.\n/// This is necessary because signal handlers run in a separate context and\n/// cannot easily access the Worker's shutdown flag directly.\n#[cfg(unix)]\nstatic GLOBAL_SHUTDOWN_FLAG: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);\n\n/// Set the global shutdown flag pointer.\n/// Called by `install_signal_handlers` to register the shutdown flag.\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn set_global_shutdown_flag(ptr: usize) {\n    GLOBAL_SHUTDOWN_FLAG.store(ptr, AtomicOrdering::SeqCst);\n}\n\n/// Clear the global shutdown flag pointer.\n/// Called when the worker is dropped to avoid dangling pointers.\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn clear_global_shutdown_flag() {\n    GLOBAL_SHUTDOWN_FLAG.store(0, AtomicOrdering::SeqCst);\n    LAST_SIGNAL.store(0, AtomicOrdering::SeqCst);\n}\n\n/// Track the last received signal for diagnostic logging.\n/// AtomicU32 allows lock-free reads/writes from the signal handler.\n#[cfg(unix)]\nstatic LAST_SIGNAL: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);\n\n/// Synchronous signal handler for SIGTERM, SIGINT, and SIGHUP.\n///\n/// This function is called directly by the OS when a signal is received.\n/// It must be async-signal-safe: no allocation, no locking, no I/O.\n/// We set the atomic shutdown flag, record the signal number, and return immediately.\n#[cfg(unix)]\nextern \"C\" fn signal_handler(sig: i32) {\n    // SAFETY: The signal handler is only installed after set_global_shutdown_flag\n    // has been called with a valid pointer. The pointer remains valid for the\n    // entire lifetime of the worker process.\n    let ptr = GLOBAL_SHUTDOWN_FLAG.load(AtomicOrdering::SeqCst) as *const AtomicBool;\n    if !ptr.is_null() {\n        // SAFETY: The pointer is valid and points to an AtomicBool that lives\n        // for the entire program duration.\n        unsafe {\n            (*ptr).store(true, AtomicOrdering::SeqCst);\n        }\n        // Record the signal number so the main loop can log it.\n        LAST_SIGNAL.store(sig as u32, AtomicOrdering::SeqCst);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Install synchronous signal handlers for SIGTERM, SIGINT, and SIGHUP.\n///\n/// Uses libc::sigaction to register handlers that set the shutdown flag\n/// immediately when a signal is received. This ensures that signals are\n/// caught even if the tokio runtime hasn't polled async signal tasks yet.\n#[cfg(unix)]\nunsafe fn install_unix_signal_handlers() {\n    use libc::{sigaction, sigemptyset, SA_RESTART, SIGHUP, SIGINT, SIGTERM};\n\n    // Set up the sigaction structure.\n    let mut act: libc::sigaction = std::mem::zeroed();\n    act.sa_sigaction = signal_handler as *const () as usize;\n    // Block all signals during handler execution to prevent re-entrancy issues.\n    sigemptyset(&mut act.sa_mask as *mut libc::sigset_t);\n    // Use SA_RESTART to automatically restart system calls interrupted by signals.\n    act.sa_flags = SA_RESTART;\n\n    // Install handlers for SIGTERM, SIGINT, and SIGHUP.\n    // We ignore errors here - if a handler can't be installed, we'll log a\n    // warning but continue. The async handlers (below) provide a fallback.\n    for &sig in &[SIGTERM, SIGINT, SIGHUP] {\n        let mut old: libc::sigaction = std::mem::zeroed();\n        if sigaction(sig, &act, &mut old) == 0 {\n            tracing::debug!(signal = sig, \"installed synchronous signal handler\");\n        } else {\n            // Log the error but don't fail - the async handlers provide a fallback.\n            #[cfg(target_os = \"linux\")]\n            let errno = unsafe { *libc::__errno_location() };\n            #[cfg(target_os = \"macos\")]\n            let errno = unsafe { *libc::__error() };\n            tracing::warn!(\n                signal = sig,\n                errno = errno,\n                \"failed to install synchronous signal handler\"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Global state for atexit handler to emit worker.stopped on unexpected termination.\n///\n/// When a worker is killed externally (e.g., SIGKILL from capacity governor),\n/// the normal signal handlers don't run. The atexit handler provides a last-resort\n/// mechanism to emit worker.stopped telemetry with diagnostic information.\nstatic ATEXIT_WORKER_STATE: Mutex<Option<AtexitWorkerState>> = Mutex::new(None);\n\n/// State captured for the atexit handler.\nstruct AtexitWorkerState {\n    worker_name: String,\n    beads_processed: u64,\n    start_time: Instant,\n    last_state: String,\n    log_file_path: Option<String>,\n    /// Path to this worker's heartbeat file for cleanup on unexpected termination.\n    heartbeat_path: Option<String>,\n}\n\n/// Register the atexit handler with worker state.\n///\n/// Called by `install_signal_handlers` to ensure the atexit handler can\n/// emit meaningful telemetry if the process terminates unexpectedly.\nfn register_atexit_handler(\n    worker_name: String,\n    beads_processed: u64,\n    start_time: Instant,\n    last_state: String,\n    log_file_path: Option<String>,\n    heartbeat_path: Option<String>,\n) {\n    let state = AtexitWorkerState {\n        worker_name,\n        beads_processed,\n        start_time,\n        last_state,\n        log_file_path,\n        heartbeat_path,\n    };\n    *ATEXIT_WORKER_STATE.lock().unwrap() = Some(state);\n\n    // Register the atexit handler.\n    // This will run when the process exits normally, but NOT on SIGKILL.\n    extern \"C\" fn atexit_handler() {\n        if let Some(state) = ATEXIT_WORKER_STATE.lock().unwrap().as_ref() {\n            let uptime = state.start_time.elapsed().as_secs();\n            // Try to write to stderr as a last resort since telemetry may be unavailable.\n            eprintln!(\n                \"NEEDLE worker '{}' stopped unexpectedly: state={}, beads_processed={}, uptime={}s\",\n                state.worker_name, state.last_state, state.beads_processed, uptime\n            );\n            eprintln!(\"This indicates the worker was killed by an external process (e.g., SIGKILL, OOM, capacity governor)\");\n\n            // Try to clean up the heartbeat file to prevent stale detection.\n            //\n            // NOTE: deliberately NOT calling crate::health::cleanup_heartbeat_file()\n            // here. This is a C `atexit` callback fired from libc's exit() — by the\n            // time it runs, Rust's thread-locals may already be torn down. That\n            // function calls tracing::debug!/warn! internally, and dispatching a\n            // tracing event needs thread-local state; if it's gone, the access\n            // panics (\"thread-local ... already destroyed\"). A panic inside an\n            // atexit handler can't unwind (\"fatal runtime error: failed to initiate\n            // panic, error 5, aborting\") and hard-aborts the whole process — this\n            // was the root cause of a recurring SIGABRT crash (lab, 2026-07-09,\n            // 261 coredumps) whenever a worker's graceful shutdown had already\n            // removed the heartbeat file before this safety-net handler ran (the\n            // common case, not the exceptional one). Do the removal directly with\n            // only std::fs + eprintln!, neither of which touch TLS.\n            if let Some(ref hb_path) = state.heartbeat_path {\n                use std::path::Path;\n                match std::fs::remove_file(Path::new(hb_path)) {\n                    Ok(_) => eprintln!(\"Cleaned up heartbeat file: {}\", hb_path),\n                    Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {\n                        eprintln!(\"Heartbeat file already removed: {}\", hb_path);\n                    }\n                    Err(e) => eprintln!(\"Heartbeat cleanup error: {}\", e),\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Try to write a worker.stopped event to the JSONL log file.\n            // This provides diagnostic information even when the worker is killed abruptly.\n            if let Some(ref log_path) = state.log_file_path {\n                use std::fs::OpenOptions;\n                use std::io::Write;\n\n                let event = serde_json::json!({\n                    \"event_type\": \"worker.stopped\",\n                    \"timestamp\": chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339_opts(chrono::SecondsFormat::Secs, true),\n                    \"data\": {\n                        \"worker_id\": state.worker_name,\n                        \"reason\": \"external_kill\",\n                        \"beads_processed\": state.beads_processed,\n                        \"uptime_secs\": uptime,\n                        \"final_state\": state.last_state,\n                        \"via_atexit_handler\": true\n                    }\n                });\n\n                if let Ok(mut file) = OpenOptions::new().create(true).append(true).open(log_path) {\n                    let _ = writeln!(file, \"{}\", event);\n                    let _ = file.flush();\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // SAFETY: atexit is safe to call with a function pointer.\n    unsafe {\n        libc::atexit(atexit_handler);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Update the atexit state when the worker state changes.\n///\n/// Called by `set_state` to keep the atexit handler's last state fresh.\nfn update_atexit_state(last_state: String) {\n    if let Some(state) = ATEXIT_WORKER_STATE.lock().unwrap().as_mut() {\n        state.last_state = last_state;\n    }\n}\n\n/// Disarm the last-resort exit report after graceful shutdown has completed.\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn clear_atexit_state() {\n    *ATEXIT_WORKER_STATE.lock().unwrap() = None;\n}\n\n/// Stub implementations for non-Unix platforms.\n/// These functions are no-ops on platforms where Unix signals are not available.\n#[cfg(not(unix))]\nfn set_global_shutdown_flag(_ptr: usize) {\n    // No-op on non-Unix platforms\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(unix))]\nfn clear_global_shutdown_flag() {\n    // No-op on non-Unix platforms\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(unix))]\nfn register_atexit_handler(\n    _worker_name: String,\n platforms\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(unix))]\nfn update_atexit_state(_last_state: String) {\n    // No-op on non-Unix platforms\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(unix))]\nfn clear_atexit_state() {\n    // No-op on non-Unix platforms\n}\n\n/// TTL for race-lost bead exclusions.\n///\n/// After losing a claim race, a bead is excluded from selection for this duration\n/// to prevent infinite loops where the selector 0.0 && worker.config.budget.stop_usd <= 0.0 {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                warn_usd = 0.0,\n                stop_usd = 0.0,\n                \"Budget enforcement is DISABLED: both warn_usd and stop_usd are set to 0.0. \\\n                 Daily spend is fully uncapped — no warnings, no halting. \\\n                 To enable budget protection, set non-zero values in .needle.yaml under 'budget:' \\\n                 (e.g., 'budget: {{warn_usd: 10.0, stop_usd: 50.0}}'). \\\n                 For fleet-wide governance, consider claude-governor (https://github.com/jedarden/claude-governor).\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        worker\n    }\n\n    /// Start the watchdog thread that monitors HANDLING state duration.\n    ///\n    /// The watchdog runs in a separate thread (not part of the Tokio runtime)\n    /// and can detect when the worker is stuck in HANDLING state even if\n    /// the Tokio runtime becomes wedged. If HANDLING state exceeds the\n    /// timeout, the watchdog sets the `watchdog_triggered` flag, which\n    /// the main worker loop checks to force recovery.\n    fn start_watchdog_thread(&mut self) {\n        let watchdog_triggered = self.watchdog_triggered.clone();\n        let handling_state_entered_at_ptr =\n            &self.handling_state_entered_at as *const Option<Instant> as usize;\n\n        let handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {\n            loop {\n                std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(5));\n                if watchdog_triggered.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {\n                    // Watchdog has already triggered, exit the thread.\n                    break;\n                }\n                // Check if we've been in HANDLING state for too long.\n                // We read the timestamp from the Worker struct via the pointer.\n                // SAFETY: The Worker struct outlives the watchdog thread because\n                // the thread is joined when the Worker is dropped.\n                let entered_at = unsafe {\n                    let ptr = handling_state_entered_at_ptr as *const Option<Instant>;\n                    (*ptr).as_ref().copied()\n                };\n\n                if let Some(entry_time) = entered_at {\n                    let elapsed = entry_time.elapsed().as_secs();\n                    if elapsed >= HANDLING_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT_SECS {\n                        tracing::error!(\n                            elapsed_secs = elapsed,\n                            \"HANDLING state watchdog triggered - forcing recovery\"\n                        );\n                        watchdog_triggered.store(true, Ordering::Release);\n                        break;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        });\n\n        self.watchdog_handle = Some(handle);\n    }\n\n    /// Run the worker loop until exhausted, stopped, or errored.\n    ///\n    /// The main loop is a match on `self.state`. Every state has a handler\n    /// that performs its actions and sets `self.state` to the next state.\n    ///\n    /// Guarantees that the telemetry BufWriter is flushed before returning,\n    /// even when the inner state machine exits early via `?`.\n    pub async fn run(&mut self) -> Result<WorkerState> {\n        // Start the telemetry writer now that we are inside the tokio runtime.\n        self.telemetry.start();\n\n        // IMMEDIATE boot event — must be the first thing emitted after telemetry starts.\n        // This ensures we get a trace even if subsequent init steps block indefinitely.\n        // Skip if already emitted externally (e.g., from CLI layer for early boot diagnostics).\n        if !self.booting_emitted {\n            self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::WorkerBooting {\n                worker_name: self.worker_name.clone(),\n                version: env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\").to_string(),\n            })?;\n            // Force-flush to disk before boot() — if init blocks, we still have a trace.\n            self.telemetry\n                .force_flush_async(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))\n                .await?;\n        }\n\n        let result = self.run_inner().await;\n\n        // Safety-net flush: shutdown() is idempotent. Normal terminal paths\n        // (stop, handle_exhausted, Errored) already call it; this catches\n        // any early-exit via `?` (boot failure, state handler panic, etc.)\n        // so the BufWriter is always flushed before the tokio Runtime drops.\n        self.telemetry.shutdown().await;\n\n        result\n    }\n\n    /// Inner state machine — called only from [`run()`](Self::run).\n    ///\n    /// May return early via `?` without calling `telemetry.shutdown()`;\n    /// `run()` handles the safety-net flush.\n    async fn run_inner(&mut self) -> Result<WorkerState> {\n        // Boot: validate config and initialize.\n        self.boot()?;\n\n        // Step: Spawn-path binary metadata recording\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::InitStepStarted {\n            step: \"spawn_path_metadata\".to_string(),\n        })?;\n        let step_start = Instant::now();\n\n        // Record spawn-path binary metadata at boot time\n        match crate::spawn_path::check_spawn_path_at_boot(None, |event| {\n            // Emit telemetry event if modification was detected\n            let old_metadata_json =\n                serde_json::to_value(&event.old_metadata).unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null);\n            let new_metadata_json =\n                serde_json::to_value(&event.new_metadata).unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null);\n\n            let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SpawnPathModifiedInPlace {\n                path: event.path,\n                old_metadata: old_metadata_json,\n                new_metadata: new_metadata_json,\n                modification_type: event.modification_type,\n                description: event.description,\n            });\n        }) {\n            Ok(metadata) => {\n                let path = metadata.path.clone();\n                let inode = metadata.inode;\n                let mtime_secs = metadata.mtime_secs;\n                let size = metadata.size;\n                let hash_preview = String::from(&metadata.hash[..16]);\n                self.spawn_path_metadata = Some(metadata);\n                tracing::info!(\n                    path = %path.display(),\n                    inode = inode,\n                    mtime_secs = mtime_secs,\n                    size = size,\n                    hash = %hash_preview,\n                    \"recorded spawn-path binary metadata\"\n                );\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                // Handle gracefully when spawn-path is not available or cannot be accessed\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to record spawn-path binary metadata, continuing without it\"\n                );\n                self.spawn_path_metadata = None;\n            }\n        }\n\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::InitStepCompleted {\n            step: \"spawn_path_metadata\".to_string(),\n            duration_ms: step_start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64,\n        })?;\n\n        // Start the watchdog thread that monitors HANDLING state duration.\n        // This must be started after boot() so the Worker struct is fully initialized.\n        self.start_watchdog_thread();\n\n        // Install signal handlers.\n        self.install_signal_handlers();\n\n        // Create the worker.session root span that encompasses the entire worker lifecycle.\n        let worker_id = self.qualified_id();\n        let workspace_name = self\n            .config\n            .workspace\n            .default\n            .file_name()\n            .and_then(|name| name.to_str())\n            .map(str::to_owned)\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| self.config.workspace.default.to_string_lossy().into_owned());\n        let session_span = tracing::info_span!(\n            \"worker.session\",\n            needle.worker_id = %worker_id,\n            needle.session_id = %self.telemetry.session_id(),\n            needle.agent = %self.config.agent.default,\n            needle.model = %self.config.agent.default, // Will be updated when adapter is resolved\n            needle.workspace = %workspace_name,\n        );\n\n        // Instrumenting the future re-enters this span on every poll. Holding an\n        // entered guard around the loop would strand its thread-local entry if the\n        // task resumed on another Tokio worker thread.\n        self.run_state_machine().instrument(session_span).await\n    }\n\n    async fn run_state_machine(&mut self) -> Result<WorkerState> {\n        loop {\n            // Check for shutdown signal between states.\n            if self.shutdown.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {\n                // Retrieve and clear the last received signal for logging.\n                #[cfg(unix)]\n                let signal_name = {\n                    let sig = LAST_SIGNAL.swap(0, AtomicOrdering::SeqCst);\n                    if sig == 0 {\n                        None\n                    } else {\n                        Some(match sig {\n                            1 => \"SIGHUP\",\n                            2 => \"SIGINT\",\n                            15 => \"SIGTERM\",\n                            _ => \"unknown signal\",\n                        })\n                    }\n                };\n                #[cfg(not(unix))]\n                let signal_name = None;\n\n                let reason = if let Some(name) = signal_name {\n                    format!(\"signal received ({name})\")\n                } else {\n                    \"signal received\".to_string()\n                };\n\n                match self.state {\n                    // If we're in the middle of processing a bead, release it\n                    // before stopping. This ensures the bead is returned to\n                    // the open state and can be claimed by another worker.\n                    WorkerState::Building\n                    | WorkerState::Dispatching\n                    | WorkerState::Executing\n                    | WorkerState::Handling => {\n                        // Release any claimed bead before stopping.\n                        self.release_current_bead(&reason).await;\n                        return self.stop(&reason).await;\n                    }\n                    // For states where we don't hold a bead, stop immediately.\n                    WorkerState::Selecting\n                    | WorkerState::Claiming\n                    | WorkerState::Retrying\n                    | WorkerState::Logging => {\n                        // Release any claimed bead before stopping (should be none in these states).\n                        self.release_current_bead(&reason).await;\n                        return self.stop(&reason).await;\n                    }\n                    WorkerState::Stopped | WorkerState::Exhausted | WorkerState::Errored => {\n                        return self.stop(&reason).await;\n                    }\n                    WorkerState::Booting => {\n                        return self.stop(\"signal received during boot\").await;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Check for watchdog trigger - this indicates HANDLING state is wedged.\n            // The watchdog runs in a separate thread and can detect when the worker\n            // is stuck even if the Tokio runtime becomes unresponsive.\n            if self.watchdog_triggered.load(Ordering::Relaxed)\n                && self.state == WorkerState::Handling\n            {\n                tracing::error!(\"watchdog detected HANDLING state hang, forcing recovery\");\n                // Emit critical timeout event.\n                let bead_id = self.current_bead.as_ref().map(|b| b.id.clone());\n                let _ = self\n                    .telemetry\n                    .emit_try_lock(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| BeadId::from(\"unknown\")),\n                        outcome: \"unknown\".to_string(),\n                        operation: \"watchdog\".to_string(),\n                        error: format!(\n                            \"HANDLING state exceeded {}s timeout\",\n                            HANDLING_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT_SECS\n                        ),\n                    });\n                // Attempt best-effort release if we have a bead.\n                if let Some(ref bead) = self.current_bead {\n                    let bead_id = bead.id.clone();\n                    tracing::warn!(bead_id = %bead_id, \"best-effort bead release due to watchdog timeout\");\n                    let _ =\n                        tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(30), self.store.release(&bead_id))\n                            .await;\n                }\n                // Clear the watchdog trigger and force transition to LOGGING.\n                self.watchdog_triggered.store(false, Ordering::Release);\n                self.handling_state_entered_at = None;\n                // Force transition to LOGGING to recover.\n                self.set_state(WorkerState::Logging)?;\n            }\n\n            // A plain `Span` handle is safe to clone and move between threads. Each\n            // bead-processing handler is instrumented separately so its polls and\n            // synchronous tracing events see the lifecycle span as current without\n            // keeping a thread-local entry alive between polls.\n            let lifecycle_span = self\n                .bead_lifecycle_span\n                .clone()\n                .unwrap_or_else(tracing::Span::none);\n\n            match self.state {\n                WorkerState::Selecting => self.do_select().await?,\n                WorkerState::Claiming => self.do_claim().await?,\n                WorkerState::Retrying => self.do_retry().await?,\n                WorkerState::Building => self.do_build().instrument(lifecycle_span.clone()).await?,\n                WorkerState::Dispatching => {\n                    self.do_dispatch()\n                        .instrument(lifecycle_span.clone())\n                        .await?\n                }\n                WorkerState::Executing => {\n                    self.do_execute().instrument(lifecycle_span.clone()).await?\n                }\n                WorkerState::Handling => {\n                    self.do_handle().instrument(lifecycle_span.clone()).await?\n                }\n                WorkerState::Logging => {\n                    lifecycle_span.in_scope(|| self.do_log())?;\n\n                    // After logging completes, check if the running binary is stale\n                    // compared to the latest needle-stable on disk. If a newer binary\n                    // is detected, exit cleanly so a supervisor or relaunch can pick\n                    // up the new binary. This check runs between dispatch cycles,\n                    // never mid-claim, ensuring no bead is left in_progress.\n                    if let Err(e) = self.check_hot_reload().await {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            error = %e,\n                            \"hot-reload check failed, continuing on current binary\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                    // If check_hot_reload() detected a new binary and successfully\n                    // re-execed, we won't reach here (the process is replaced).\n                    // On re-exec failure, we continue normally.\n                }\n                WorkerState::Exhausted => {\n                    let next = self.handle_exhausted().await?;\n                    match next {\n                        WorkerState::Selecting => continue,\n                        terminal => return Ok(terminal),\n                    }\n                }\n                WorkerState::Stopped => {\n                    return self.stop(\"normal shutdown\").await;\n                }\n                WorkerState::Errored => {\n                    let err = self\n                        .last_error\n                        .take()\n                        .unwrap_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"unknown error\"));\n                    let msg = format!(\"{err}\");\n                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::WorkerErrored {\n                        error_type: \"worker_scoped\".to_string(),\n                        error_message: msg.clone(),\n                        beads_processed: self.beads_processed,\n                    })?;\n\n                    // Emit WorkerStopped before exiting so telemetry shows a clean shutdown.\n                    // This ensures operators can distinguish \"exited with error\" from\n                    // \"killed by external agent\" (e.g., SIGKILL, OOM).\n                    let uptime = self.boot_time.map(|t| t.elapsed().as_secs()).unwrap_or(0);\n                    let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::WorkerStopped {\n                        reason: format!(\"error: {msg}\"),\n                        beads_processed: self.beads_processed,\n                        uptime_secs: uptime,\n                    });\n\n                    // Best-effort stop heartbeat on error.\n                    self.health.stop();\n                    // Best-effort deregister on error.\n                    if let Err(e) = self.registry.deregister(&self.qualified_id()) {\n                        tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"failed to deregister from worker registry on error\");\n                    }\n                    self.telemetry.shutdown().await;\n                    return Err(err);\n                }\n                WorkerState::Booting => {\n                    bail!(\"boot() should have transitioned past Booting state\");\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ── Boot ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Validate configuration and initialize the worker.\n    ///\n    /// Each step is instrumented with
